content.body:
## Problem and people

Conversation Lab proposes optional practice for first-time team leads using an invented missed-handoff story. A handoff note was absent on Monday, the next shift repeated a check, and the lead has not heard the colleague's account. The task is to distinguish observation from explanation, choose an opening, reconsider after additional context, and prepare a feasible conversation proposal. The missing note establishes neither carelessness nor responsibility for the repeated check; their causal relationship is unknown.

New leads, colleagues, managers, learning teams and employee representatives are prospective affected groups. None have participated. This integrated Design brief is a provisional synthesis for a rehearsal candidate, not approved requirements or demonstrated professional proficiency.

Sequence 2 is an actual preservation verification event. It preserves parent framing, Map and Design as background, including a hypothetical staffing interruption: tentative practice wording remains visible on a shared workstation and a supervisor associates it with capability. That interruption was not observed. The previous workforce journal remains an immutable parent, not a measured baseline or approved intervention. Sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13 supply specialist drafts rather than participant evidence.

Rival explanations for the workplace concern include changed schedules, inaccessible tools, unclear ownership, inadequate coverage and conflicting expectations. Conversation difficulty could be secondary to these conditions. Training is not the automatic response.

## Human and system capability

Human capability: participants need room to question observations, retain tentative interpretations, reject suggestions, withhold agreement, choose written participation, pass or stop without giving a reason. Leads must distinguish their own inquiry from changes requiring another person's authority. Managers must inspect staffing, protected time, workflow access, ownership and suitable space. Facilitators need covered time and must accommodate access needs without judging speech, confidence, speed, eye contact or script fidelity. No support owners, resources or participation protections are secured.

System capability: a deterministic browser activity will assemble explicitly authored fictional material and participant-selected proposals. It will not predict reactions, evaluate optional text, diagnose learning needs, infer consent or assess readiness. Keep supplied facts, tentative explanations, missing accounts, historical wording, current proposals and pending replacements distinct. Every proposed next move must carry relevant support, authority, unassigned work and unresolved agreement.

Use fictional inputs only. Exclude real employee records, identifiable recordings, profiling, ranking, consequential HR advice, automatic scores, telemetry, storage and network requests. Maintain only volatile state within the candidate frame; refresh or closure loses work. No export, sharing, certificate, attendance log, aid-use count or participant analytics is proposed. Humans retain all consequential workplace decisions and any separate decision to disclose material.

Language preferences, reading demands, devices, assistive technology, suitable space and coverage are unknown. Responsive layout, plain wording, visible focus and untimed keyboard operation are intended qualities to inspect, not established access. Recording nothing cannot prevent informal observation or employment pressure.

## Experience and decisions

The primary task is one conversation proposal, not a reflection questionnaire. Start with a compact situation board in linear reading order: Observed fictional facts, Possible explanations and Missing context. Show Monday's absent note and the repeated check as observations; show process, access or priority explanations as tentative; keep the unheard colleague account and uncertain causal relationship visible. Selecting an explanation never promotes it into a fact. Do not depend on dragging, color, hover or visual position.

Offer three openings with exact previews: “I noticed Monday's handoff note was absent. What was happening from your perspective?”; “Can we check how the handoff was meant to work on Monday?”; and “I need more context before deciding our next step.” The learner chooses an opening and a provisional next move through brief choices. Blank optional fields must still yield a useful initial proposal. Pass, Stop, Cover and Paper activity remain available without justification. Explain session loss before entry; keep detailed review metadata in Help.

Each opening changes an explicitly authored possible exchange and its descriptive implications. Provide possibilities in which the colleague offers context, questions an interpretation or requests a later discussion. Label these beside the dialogue as invented possibilities, not predictions or evidence about people. Participants may reject an example and continue with the account unresolved.

Capture the initial proposal, then reveal the supplied fictional context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague, and the expected owner was unclear. The reveal adds information without establishing a complete cause. Invite retaining or revising the interpretation and next move; neither receives praise, blame or a correctness label. Retained wording must still display the new constraints.

Offer next moves such as checking the current expectation, requesting support before proposing template use, or pausing until a suitable conversation is possible. Reveal relevant dependency choices only when needed. Unknown or unavailable support produces a conditional next move, a support inquiry or a pause, never an unconditional promise. Show whose authority would be needed without assigning an owner or repair work automatically. Even available fictional support leaves colleague agreement unresolved.

Preserve historical source facts. A later selection of available support means a hypothetical future condition for the proposed move; it must not rewrite Monday's inaccessible template or unclear owner. Label that distinction explicitly. The optional second situation has separate source data and must not inherit these facts.

Feedback describes what the selected wording states, whose account it invites and what remains unresolved. For a carelessness interpretation, distinguish the observed absence from its uncertain reason. For template use, name unresolved access and ownership. For a process inquiry, name the expectation being checked. For postponement, show that agreement is deferred and a suitable opportunity or support remains to be arranged. Feedback is contestable. Participants may reject it, retain a proposal or revise one component. An optional focused retry previews another authored possibility; it makes no claim that revision improves real conversations.

Show clearly labelled Initial proposal and Current proposal, including observation, invitation, next move, needed support, authority, unassigned work and unresolved questions or disagreement. State what changed or was retained neutrally. Keep “Fictional practice proposal; no workplace agreement or capability judgment” beside the output. A narrow layout may show versions sequentially while preserving their labels.

Use at most two optional main-path text fields: replacement wording and an unresolved question, both labelled for fictional content only. Correction shows the exact replacement, affected component and dependency summary before Apply or Cancel. Cancel preserves the current proposal. A relevant context or support change invalidates pending review and requires renewed inspection before Apply. Participant wording remains verbatim and labelled; the candidate cannot certify its feasibility. Support and agreement conditions remain independently visible even if entered wording contradicts them.

Cover immediately conceals all candidate content surfaces, including history, current plans, optional text, pending replacements, dialogue, second-situation content and open detail views. Concealed material must be unavailable through ordinary assistive-technology navigation. Move focus to a neutral screen. Explicit Resume restores the corrected state and offers optional orientation without requiring recall. No automatic resumption, inactivity scoring or interruption logs.

Finish and clear for handoff is separate from Cover. Review its scope and require confirmation; Cancel retains the session. Confirmation removes all candidate session values and rendered content, including both situations, selections, drafts, history and pending previews, then presents a neutral start state. Clearing must work from Cover without exposing content. Concealment retains volatile work; clearing removes candidate state. Neither prevents prior viewing, external capture or inspection beyond the candidate's control.

Offer one optional second fictional situation: “Two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check.” Begin with fewer suggestions, keeping help immediately available and recording no aid use. Use an opening and next move addressing disputed ownership; do not import the first situation's access barrier. Call this supported practice, never a transfer test or evidence of greater competence.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Inquiry, feedback and reciprocal agency. Origins: Workforce R1/R3 in sequence 5; Systems SE2 in sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD1/HCD2 in sequence 9; Learning scientist LS1–LS3 in sequence 11. Interaction: a labelled situation board, choice-specific authored previews, contestable descriptive feedback, fictional reveal, optional focused retry and correctable before/after proposal. Human reason: participants need to examine ambiguity and hear a missing perspective without conforming to a script. System reason: a polished preview can otherwise appear to diagnose the problem or predict a colleague. Acceptance: complete the task without typing, reject examples and feedback, retain a tentative interpretation after the reveal, and finish with unresolved disagreement or a pause; no score, agreement or readiness inference appears. Check the second situation retains only its supplied facts and remains supported practice. Task relevance, feedback criteria and access remain unreviewed.

R2 — Feasible support without delegated authority. Origins: Workforce R2 in sequence 5; Systems SE1 in sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD3 in sequence 9; Responsible AI RA1 in sequence 13. Interaction: choosing a dependent next move exposes support and authority, qualifies its wording and shows work still unassigned. Human reason: a lead cannot promise access repair, allocate another person's work or obtain agreement through a selection. System reason: dependency labels alone can coexist with an infeasible commitment. Acceptance: inaccessible template plus unclear ownership yields inquiry, a conditional proposal or pause; it never assigns repair or states unconditional use. Changing a prospective support condition leaves historical facts intact and requires renewed review of a pending replacement. Available support never implies colleague consent. Real resources and authority remain unknown.

R3 — Participant control, recovery and equivalent alternatives. Origins: the hypothetical interruption preserved by sequence 2; Workforce R4/R5 in sequence 5; Systems SE3/SE4 in sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD4/HCD5 in sequence 9; Learning scientist LS4 in sequence 11; Responsible AI RA2–RA4 in sequence 13. Interaction: exact Apply/Cancel, persistent Cover, explicit Resume with optional orientation, confirmed complete clearing and directly available paper materials. Human reason: interruption, dissent and device handoff require different voluntary decisions; recovery must not test memory. System reason: stale drafts, open Help and partial resets can expose or restore rejected content. Acceptance: apply one correction, cancel another, cover all surfaces by keyboard, resume the corrected state, cancel clearing, then confirm clearing from Cover and inspect a complete reset. Inspect focus, narrow layout, concealed accessibility content and absence of network, storage or tracking. Run the equivalent paper task without the browser. No checks have occurred; workplace privacy and credible refusal require human review.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Choices reduce writing burden but constrain expression; optional replacement and unresolved dissent preserve correction without requiring an essay. Examples support entry but can encourage imitation; rejecting them and requesting support remain legitimate. Support detail improves feasibility but adds work, so reveal it when the proposed move requires it. Before/after comparison makes revision visible without making revision the goal.

Retain dissent that workflow repair or no practice is preferable. Clarifying ownership, restoring accessible materials, inspecting the rota and arranging coverage are non-learning options requiring human authority. A deterministic browser activity is a non-AI option; facilitated paper practice is a complete alternative. Neither can secure participation protections or authorize organizational change.

Paper materials: situation card with the three initial story statements; board labelled Observed facts, Possible explanations and Missing context; the three exact opening cards above; blank replacement, Pass and Stop cards. Add a reveal card stating the changed rota, inaccessible template and unclear expected owner, labelled invented context rather than a complete explanation. Add authored response cards: “Here is additional context”, “I question that interpretation” and “I would prefer to discuss this later”; label them possibilities rather than predictions.

Provide Initial proposal and Current proposal sheets with spaces for observation, invitation, next move, support, authority, unassigned work and unresolved disagreement. Supply support cards Unknown, Unavailable and Available for the proposed fictional next move, a reminder that agreement remains unresolved, and a feedback card asking: “Which wording is observation or explanation?”, “Whose account or agreement is missing?” and “What support makes this move feasible?” Include a blank cover sheet and the exact second-situation card above; make opening suggestions available on request.

Facilitation: first arrange voluntary participation, protected time, accessible materials, suitable space and participant-controlled disposal. Present the situation and invite an opening or Pass; written selection is sufficient. Record the initial proposal, release the reveal, describe dependencies without grading and invite retaining or revising one component. Review the exact replacement before accepting it; cancellation keeps the current sheet. Leave disagreement and unassigned work visible. Offer a response-card retry, the second situation or stopping. Speech and role-play are optional. Do not solicit personal accounts, collect or photograph sheets, grade aid use, record attendance for assessment or require sharing. Cover for interruption and resume only by participant choice. Dispose of sheets under the agreed arrangement. These conditions have not been secured.

## Acceptance checks

Prepare fictional task walkthroughs for every opening, disputed interpretation, unavailable support, unclear authority, postponement and rejected feedback. Inspect concrete output with blank optional fields and faithful source distinctions. Compare retained and revised proposals without treating either as success.

Prepare recovery walkthroughs containing history, an applied correction, a cancelled replacement, a pending review, open Help and second-situation progress. Inspect renewed review after changed conditions, keyboard focus, concealment, accurate resumption and complete confirmed clearing. Separately inspect code and runtime for prohibited storage, network requests and tracking. These are planned checks, not observed behavior.

Practitioner, affected-person and representative review must separately examine comprehension, reciprocal dignity, language, device access, credible refusal, workload, privacy and paper handling. Technical verification establishes only the behavior inspected. It cannot establish free participation, learning, retention, transfer or flourishing.

## Evidence and unknowns

Actual references are sequence 2's preservation verification and Design drafts 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. The interruption is hypothetical; the seed supplies invented source material. No participant observations, consensus, human approval, technical results, field pilot or empirical success exist. Field evidence remains pending.

Changes after the interruption are complete participant-controlled concealment, correction-aware resumption without recall, and distinct confirmed handoff clearing. This synthesis additionally binds proposal wording to support, preserves workload and agreement boundaries, and distinguishes supported practice from transfer. These refine current Design; no named earlier requirement is invalidated, so Understand and Map remain preserved.

Unknowns include whether this is an important learning need, whether choices and feedback represent affected perspectives, whether refusal is credible and whether feasible support exists. Later apparent improvement could reflect copied examples, familiarity, facilitator cues, selective participation, repaired workflow or stronger managerial support. Difficulty could reflect reading, language, workload or dissent rather than a capability deficit. Delayed retention and adaptation to changed workplace conditions require separate reviewed evidence; they are outside this candidate's claims.

## Next decision

Proceed to a focused rehearsal Build implementing this brief with fictional data and deterministic interactions. Then perform the proposed technical walkthroughs and prepare practitioner and affected-person interaction review. Keep intended quality, observed technical behavior and untested learning, transfer and flourishing separate. Any later field-use decision requires accountable human review of participation, staffing, authority, access and privacy; no approval or launch authority exists here.

Conversation Lab proposes fictional practice for first-time team leads. The supplied story states that a handoff note was absent on Monday, the next shift repeated a check, and the lead has not heard the colleague’s account. The intended task is to distinguish observations from explanations, choose an opening, reconsider after additional context and construct a feasible conversation proposal. The absent note does not establish carelessness, responsibility or the cause of the repeated check.

New leads, colleagues, managers, learning teams and employee representatives are prospective affected groups. None have participated. This Human-centered designer contribution is an expert draft for Design synthesis, not an approved requirement.

Sequence 2 explicitly preserves the parent framing, Map and Design as background. Its parent Design includes a hypothetical interruption: a lead is recalled to cover a staffing gap while tentative practice wording remains visible on a shared workstation. No such incident was observed. Sequences 5 and 7 carry this concern into cover/resume, correction and complete clearing requirements.

The discipline-specific challenge is that technical correction and feasible dependencies are insufficient if the experience still centers the lead’s interpretation, treats suggested wording as obligatory or allocates organizational repair to the colleague. The interface must expose whose account is missing, whose agreement remains absent and who would bear proposed work.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: participants need discretion to choose a written route, decline an example, pass, stop or leave disagreement unresolved without explaining why. Leads need to recognize the boundary between proposing an action and obtaining another person’s agreement. Managers must inspect protected time, staffing, suitable space, accessible workflow materials and authority before expecting participation or repair. Facilitators need time and support to accommodate different access needs without judging speed, speech, confidence or script conformity.

System requirements: provide a usable plan through choices and concrete previews without mandatory text entry. Keep fictional observations, possible explanations, missing accounts and unaccepted proposals distinct. Show relevant support and authority alongside the next move. Do not infer consent, capability, readiness or a colleague’s likely response from a selection.

The candidate must use fictional inputs only and exclude employee ranking, consequential HR advice, identifiable recordings, profiling, telemetry, storage and network requests. Recovery is confined to the current volatile session; refresh or closure loses work. No implementation has been inspected.

Language preferences, literacy demands, device availability, assistive technology, time, suitable space and participation protections are unknown. Plain wording, responsive layout and keyboard support are intended qualities requiring technical inspection and affected-person review. They do not establish accessibility for everyone.

## Experience and decisions

Open with a short situation board in a consistent reading order: Observed fictional facts, Possible explanations, Missing context. Do not require dragging cards, recognizing color or hovering. Explanation cards remain visibly tentative; selecting one does not move it into the facts area. Keep the colleague’s unheard account visible throughout.

Offer three concrete openings: an observation with an invitation, a question about the handoff process, and a decision to pause while checking context. Pass, Stop and Paper activity remain available without a justification field. Explain before entry that nothing is scored or shared and that work disappears on refresh or closure. Put detailed review information in Help.

Choosing an opening displays exact wording and explicitly authored possible dialogue. Include possibilities in which the colleague explains context, questions the interpretation or asks to discuss it later. These are invented examples, not predicted reactions. The participant can choose another opening, reject the example or continue with the account unresolved. No branch is marked as the correct response.

Reveal the supplied additional fictional context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague and the expected owner was unclear. Retaining or revising the initial interpretation are both legitimate. Describe which uncertainties and dependencies remain; do not praise revision itself or treat the reveal as a complete diagnosis.

Build a proposal comprising an observation, an invitation and a next move. When the participant chooses template use, reveal access and ownership conditions. If support is unknown or unavailable, offer requesting support, choosing another move or pausing. Display who would need to authorize a change and which work remains unassigned. Do not make the colleague responsible for fixing the inaccessible template by default. Even fictional support marked available leaves colleague agreement unresolved.

Show an Initial proposal and a Current proposal with an explicit statement of what changed or that the participant retained the original. Keep unresolved questions and support visible. A comparison need not appear simultaneously on a narrow screen; each version must remain clearly labelled and accessible without relying on visual position.

At most two optional open-text fields belong on the main path: replacement wording and an unresolved question. Choices must produce a concrete output when both are blank. Correction opens a review showing the exact replacement and dependency summary, followed by Apply and Cancel. Cancel preserves current wording and support state. If context changes during review, require renewed review before applying, as proposed in sequence 7. Authored suggestions must remain distinguishable from participant wording.

Cover immediately conceals all scenario, plan, optional text and pending-review content from visual and ordinary assistive-technology access, then places focus on a neutral screen. Resume is explicit and restores the current corrected state without demanding recall or an explanation. Finish and clear is separate: describe that all current-session material will be removed, require confirmation, and allow cancellation. Clearing must be possible from the covered screen without exposing its contents. Concealment does not establish shared-device suitability or prevent prior viewing.

Offer the optional second fictional situation with fewer suggestions: two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check. Keep support available on request and permit stopping. This is supported practice, not a test or evidence of transfer.

## Requirements and rationale

HCD1 — Human-centered designer origin, extending Workforce R1 in sequence 5 and Systems SE2 in sequence 7: make the situation board usable in a linear reading order, with text labels for facts, explanations and missing context. Human reason: device, vision, motor and reading conditions must not determine who can examine ambiguity. System reason: spatial layout and color alone cannot carry meaning. Acceptance check: a reviewer using only the keyboard can inspect every category, choose an explanation and still identify it as tentative; the colleague’s account remains missing after the reveal. Supplied context is the seed’s situation board; actual access needs remain unknown.

HCD2 — Human-centered designer origin, extending Workforce R3 in sequence 5 and Systems SE2 in sequence 7: make dissent and withholding agreement visible states rather than optional prose. Provide rejection of suggested wording, postponement and an unresolved-account route. Human reason: colleagues and leads retain different perspectives and participation choices. System reason: a selected dialogue branch must not appear to settle a conversation. Acceptance check: a reviewer can reject all examples and finish with an inquiry or pause, with no agreement or capability judgment in the output. Credible workplace refusal requires affected-person review.

HCD3 — Human-centered designer origin, extending Workforce R2 in sequence 5 and Systems SE1 in sequence 7: show responsibility and unassigned work beside each support-dependent next move. Human reason: an access barrier should not automatically create repair work for the colleague. System reason: conditional wording can still conceal workload allocation. Acceptance check: selecting inaccessible template and unclear owner produces a support request or pause, displays unresolved authority and does not assign repair to anyone. Actual support owners, resources and authority are unknown.

HCD4 — Human-centered designer origin, extending the hypothetical interruption preserved in sequence 2, Workforce R4 in sequence 5 and Systems SE3 in sequence 7: make recovery understandable and independent of recall. Use a persistent Cover control, a neutral covered screen, explicit Resume and separately confirmed clearing. Human reason: interruption and staffing demands should not require a participant to reconstruct or expose tentative reflection. System reason: historical, current and pending content need complete concealment and reset coverage. Acceptance check: apply a correction, cancel another, cover by keyboard and resume; current wording remains correct and concealed content is unavailable through ordinary accessibility navigation. Confirmed clearing removes both situations and all drafts. No check has occurred.

HCD5 — Human-centered designer origin, extending Workforce R5 in sequence 5 and Systems SE4 in sequence 7: provide equivalent written and facilitated paper decisions with low entry burden. Human reason: speech, role-play, devices and extensive writing may be unsuitable. System reason: an alternative must complete the same task without the candidate. Acceptance check: a reviewer can complete the digital route with no text entry and run the paper route using the materials below, including disagreement, revision and support decisions. Language suitability and facilitation workload remain pending review.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Choices reduce entry work but constrain expression; optional replacement wording and unresolved disagreement provide correction without requiring an essay. Examples offer support but can become scripts; rejection must not trigger corrective feedback. Before/after comparison makes revision inspectable but may privilege change; retaining a proposal must receive the same neutral treatment.

Retain dissent that conversation practice is the wrong response when access, staffing or ownership are unresolved. A non-learning option is to clarify the workflow, repair template access and arrange coverage before offering voluntary practice. The candidate cannot authorize or verify these changes.

Complete non-AI materials: a situation card reading, “A handoff note was absent on Monday. The next shift repeated a check. The new lead has not heard the colleague’s account”; a board labelled Observed facts, Possible explanations and Missing context; and opening cards reading, “I noticed Monday’s handoff note was absent. What was happening from your perspective?”, “Can we check how the handoff was meant to work on Monday?” and “I need more context before deciding our next step.” Include blank replacement, Pass and Stop cards.

Provide a reveal card reading, “The rota changed. The template was inaccessible to the colleague. The expected owner was unclear. This is invented context, not a complete explanation.” Provide response cards reading, “Here is additional context”, “I question that interpretation” and “I would prefer to discuss this later”. These support written selection; speech and role-play are optional.

Provide Initial proposal and Current proposal sheets with spaces for observation, invitation, next move, needed support, authority, work still unassigned and unresolved disagreement. Add support cards labelled Unknown, Unavailable and Available in this fictional situation. Provide a blank cover sheet and an optional second-situation card reading, “Two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check.”

Facilitator instructions: first arrange voluntary participation, covered time, accessible materials, suitable space and participant-controlled disposal. Present the situation and invite an opening or Pass. Release the reveal, then invite retaining or revising the proposal. Pair the next move with support, authority and workload; leave disagreement visible. Offer the second situation with fewer suggestions or end. Do not solicit personal accounts, collect or photograph sheets, grade wording or require sharing. Use the cover sheet for interruption and resume only by participant choice. Dispose of materials under the arrangement agreed before starting. These conditions have not been secured.

## Acceptance checks

Prepare a fictional agency walkthrough: choose an opening, reject the dialogue example, reveal context, retain an interpretation and finish with a support request while the colleague’s account and agreement remain unresolved. Inspect that no correctness label, completion penalty or readiness claim appears.

Prepare an access and recovery walkthrough: complete the main task without text entry using only the keyboard, inspect a narrow layout and meaningful labels, review and cancel a correction, then cover and resume. Inspect concealed content and focus through ordinary accessibility navigation. Cancel clearing once, then confirm it from the covered screen and inspect the complete reset. These are proposed checks, not results.

Practitioner and affected-person review should examine comprehension, dignity, language, credible passing, task burden and responsibility allocation. Technical inspection should separately examine storage, network behavior, focus and state handling. Passing technical checks would establish only the behavior inspected; learning, transfer, belonging and sustainable workload remain untested.

## Evidence and unknowns

Actual references are sequence 2, the preserved-parent verification event; sequence 5, the Workforce specialist draft; and sequence 7, the Systems engineer draft. The shared-workstation interruption in sequence 2 is hypothetical. The seed supplies invented source material and constraints. No new participant observation, authorization, consensus or measured outcome exists. Field evidence remains pending.

The design change after the preserved interruption is to make recovery participant-controlled, correction-aware and usable without recall, with confirmed clearing separate from concealment. This draft additionally makes dissent a concrete interaction and exposes workload allocation. These refine current Design; no supplied evidence invalidates the earlier Map.

Unknowns include whether the task reflects an important need, whether the choices represent affected people adequately and whether protected time and accessible support are feasible. Rival explanations for later apparent benefit include facilitator cues, familiarity, selective participation, repaired workflow and stronger managerial support. Revision, completion and second-situation performance cannot establish learning or transfer.

## Next decision

Incorporate these proposed interactions and acceptance cases into the Design synthesis and subsequent candidate Build. ## Human and system capability

Human requirements: participants need discretion to question feedback, retain an interpretation as tentative, revise one part of a plan, request examples or stop. Facilitators need to distinguish a difficulty with the decision from reading demands, language preferences, unclear instructions or unavailable workflow support. Managers must examine coverage, accessible materials, ownership and authority before treating conversation practice as appropriate. Practitioners and affected people must review the proposed feedback focus: whether wording distinguishes observation from explanation, invites an account and makes the next step conditional on feasible support and agreement. These are proposed criteria, not a settled communication standard. Dissent over their usefulness must remain visible. Speed, confidence, eye contact, preferred phrasing and agreement with a facilitator are not proposed criteria.

System requirements: show the participant’s decision and its consequences in the fictional exercise. ## Experience and decisions

The meaningful first decision is how to open an inquiry: state an observation and invite an account; examine the handoff process; or pause to check missing context. Show exact wording and a clearly labelled authored possible exchange. Choosing an opening changes that preview and the questions still to resolve; it does not produce a predicted human reaction. Include disagreement and postponement possibilities without ranking them.

After the initial proposal, reveal the supplied fictional context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague and the expected owner was unclear. Ask the participant to retain or reconsider the interpretation and next move through choices. Do not require a written explanation. The reveal changes available information and the feasibility of some actions; it does not establish a complete account or mandate a particular phrase.

Display brief descriptive feedback beside the current proposal. For an interpretation such as carelessness, say that the missing note is an observation while its reason remains uncertain. For a template-dependent move, state that access and ownership remain unresolved. For a process question, identify what it seeks to clarify and what it still leaves unanswered. For postponement, show that immediate agreement is deferred and that support or a suitable opportunity remains to be arranged. Feedback should describe these implications without praise, blame or correctness labels.

Let the participant reject the feedback, retain the proposal with unresolved conditions, or revise one element: observation, invitation or next move. A focused retry means trying the revised opening against another authored possibility, such as a colleague questioning the interpretation or requesting a later discussion. Label this as another invented possibility, not evidence that revision improves a real conversation. Repetition is optional.

Produce a correctable comparison of Initial proposal and Current proposal, including what was retained, what changed, workflow dependencies and unanswered questions. Do not use revision count or the amount of changed text as progress. A participant who retains wording should receive the same neutral treatment as one who revises it. A retained next move must still display the newly revealed constraints.

Choices and previews must produce a useful plan without text entry. Keep at most two optional open-text fields on the main path: replacement wording and an unresolved question. Display exact proposed changes and their dependency summary before Apply or Cancel. Cancel preserves the current proposal. Follow sequence 7’s requirement for renewed review when relevant conditions change during a pending correction.

Cover/resume must restore the corrected state and offer an optional orientation to the current proposal. Do not require unaided recall before resumption. The interruption concern preserved in sequence 2 changes the recovery requirement: remembering after an interruption cannot become an entry condition or a competence signal. Confirmed clearing remains separate and removes every scenario, draft and pending review, including the optional second situation.

Offer the supplied second situation: two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check. Show the situation first with fewer opening suggestions, while allowing the participant to request support immediately. Invite a next move that addresses the disputed ownership rather than carrying forward assumptions about template access. Show which suggestions are available now, but do not record their use. This is another supported practice opportunity, not a transfer test.

## Requirements and rationale

LS1 — Learning scientist origin, extending Workforce R1/R3 in sequence 5, Systems SE2 in sequence 7 and HCD2 in sequence 9: connect each opening and next move to descriptive, contestable feedback. Human reason: participants need to examine a decision rather than infer a preferred answer from praise. System reason: a selected script otherwise conceals the assumption and remaining uncertainty. Interaction: show what the wording states, what account it invites and what dependency remains; allow retaining, rejecting or revising it. Acceptance check: a reviewer can choose each opening, identify its distinct implications and reject the feedback without receiving a correctness label or losing access. The seed supplies the decisions; the feedback criteria remain pending affected-person review.

LS2 — Learning scientist origin, extending the revision cycle preserved in sequence 2 and the correction rules in sequences 7 and 9: provide one optional focused retry after changed fictional context. Human reason: deliberate practice needs a decision that can be reconsidered, rather than compulsory repetition or six reflection boxes. System reason: a before/after display alone can make revision look like the outcome. Interaction: retain the initial proposal, reveal context, permit changing one component, review the exact replacement and optionally preview another authored response. Acceptance check: retaining, revising, cancelling and stopping all leave an accurate current plan; inaccessible template use remains conditional regardless of the chosen wording. No learning effect is established by this check.

LS3 — Learning scientist origin, extending the learning distinctions preserved in sequence 2 and the optional second situation in sequences 5, 7 and 9: separate supported performance, delayed retention and adaptation to changed conditions. Human reason: another prompted attempt does not establish later independent capability. System reason: reduced suggestions can become an implicit test or ranking. Interaction: label the second situation as supported practice, keep suggestions available on request and preserve new ownership uncertainty in its output. Acceptance check: the second situation does not inherit the first situation’s inaccessible-template fact, does not label fewer prompts as greater competence and does not describe completion as transfer. Later retention and workplace adaptation remain unknown.

LS4 — Learning scientist origin, responding to the hypothetical interruption preserved in sequence 2 and extending Systems SE3 and HCD4 in sequences 7 and 9: recovery must not test memory. Human reason: a participant recalled to cover work needs an understandable return, not another demand. System reason: restored historical or rejected wording could distort both the task and its interpretation. Interaction: offer optional orientation after explicit Resume and restore current corrections and unresolved support. Acceptance check: a reviewer can resume and continue without recalling the opening; cancelled wording does not reappear as current; clearing from Cover removes both situations. No interruption, technical check or recovery outcome has been observed.

Examples reduce entry burden but may encourage imitation. Keep their status visible, allow rejection and offer fewer initial suggestions in the optional second situation. Removing all support would introduce access and workload demands; support withdrawal is not a success criterion.

Feedback can make decisions inspectable but may privilege the designers’ assumptions. Preserve dissent that the proposed criteria or activity are inappropriate. Organizational repair is a legitimate alternative: inspect the rota, clarify ownership, restore template access and arrange coverage before deciding whether voluntary practice adds value. The tool cannot authorize those changes.

## Named assumption and revision scope

Challenged assumption: access and authority can be represented as available support without separately establishing protected capacity and acceptance of the associated workload.

Sequence 7 binds proposal wording to support and authority. Sequence 9 exposes unassigned work. Sequence 13 preserves consent and delegation boundaries. Sequence 15 incorporates those protections and names staffing and protected time as human conditions. However, its specified interaction does not explicitly distinguish restored access from withdrawn capacity or show what happens when those conditions conflict.

Request revision of Design, the earliest supplied artifact whose interaction specification needs this change. The supplied material does not establish that an earlier Map artifact omitted these conditions; no claim about that artifact is made.

## Concrete requirement change

SC1 — Scenario origin, extending sequence 15 R2 and R3, with dependencies from sequences 7, 9 and 13: for a next move requiring additional handoff work, represent protected time and coverage separately from access and authority. Use brief choices such as “Protected time and coverage available”, “Unavailable” and “Unknown”. Label these as fictional prospective conditions, never verified workplace resources.

Present this changed-condition card after an initial proposal exists. Preserve the initial proposal as historical wording. Show the current dependency state as “Access offered; protected capacity unavailable; colleague agreement withheld; ownership unresolved”. A selection of available access must not erase the workload conflict or produce an unconditional commitment.

Offer concrete routes to request clarification of protected capacity and ownership, reconsider the proposed move, or pause. The default authored synthesis must leave additional work unassigned and avoid promising after-shift completion. The learner may retain their wording or dissent from the feedback; independently visible conditions must continue to qualify it. Arbitrary replacement text remains participant wording and cannot be certified as feasible.

If the changed condition arrives during an exact replacement review, invalidate that review and require renewed inspection before Apply. Show the exact replacement and changed dependency summary together. Cancel preserves the current proposal. Cover and explicit Resume must preserve the capacity conflict and the colleague’s refusal; confirmed clearing must remove the added state with the rest of the session. No logs or assessment traces are added.

Human reason: usable tools and managerial authority do not supply time, coverage or another person’s agreement. System reason: a single available-support label can conceal an unsupported workload commitment.

## Observable acceptance checks

Prepare a fictional walkthrough that selects available template access, then reveals withdrawn coverage and the authored refusal. Inspect that the output distinguishes access from capacity, leaves ownership and agreement unresolved, and offers inquiry, revision or pause without automatically assigning extra work. Complete this path with both optional text fields blank.

Prepare a pending-correction walkthrough. Open an exact replacement review before the changed condition, introduce capacity withdrawal, and inspect that Apply requires renewed review. Cancel, Cover and Resume should retain the correct current wording and unresolved conditions. Confirmed clearing should reset the capacity state alongside both situations and all drafts.

Inspect that retaining wording, rejecting feedback or accepting the refusal produces no score, readiness claim or completion penalty. These are proposed checks only; none has been performed. They would establish inspected interaction behavior, not learning, free participation or sustainable workload.

## Alternatives, dissent and unknowns

Extend the existing complete facilitated paper activity in sequence 15 with one changed-condition card containing the event above and three capacity cards: Available, Unavailable and Unknown. Place capacity beside access and authority on the Current proposal sheet. Release the card after the initial proposal, invite retention, revision or stopping, and review any exact replacement before accepting it. Leave refused work unassigned. Retain the existing voluntary written route, cover sheet and participant-controlled disposal; no browser or AI is required.

Preserve dissent that organizational action should precede practice. A non-learning route is an accountable review of coverage, protected time, access and ownership. The candidate cannot authorize that review’s decisions or secure resources.

Rival explanations for the missed handoff remain changed rota, inaccessible materials, unclear ownership and conflicting expectations; this later workload condition does not prove any one cause. Apparent difficulty in the exercise could reflect ambiguous choices, reading demands or disagreement rather than deficient leadership. Unknowns include local shift arrangements, who can authorize protected time, whether refusal is credible and whether this branch adds excessive burden.

## Next decision and evidence boundary

Revise Design with SC1 before implementing this branch. Prepare the fictional acceptance cases and retain pending practitioner, affected-person and representative review. The event is hypothetical; sequences 7, 9, 13 and 15 are earlier design contributions, not empirical evidence. No approval, participant observation, technical result, field pilot, learning, transfer or flourishing evidence exists. Field evidence remains pending.

response.message: Hypothetical changed condition: after the learner drafts a template-based next move, an authorized manager offers restored access only if the colleague completes the handoff after their shift; coverage and protected time have been withdrawn. The fictional colleague declines that extra work. Access can therefore be available while the proposed move remains infeasible. Sequence 15 requires conditional proposals but does not explicitly represent this conflict as an actionable workload state. Revise Design to distinguish access, authority and supported capacity, preserve the refusal, and require renewed proposal review. This is a Scenario specialist draft, not an observed event or approved requirement. Human review and field evidence remain pending.
objections: A fictional colleague objects: “Making the template accessible does not give me time to complete it after my shift.”
Workflow repair or no practice may be preferable to rehearsing a conversation under unsupported conditions.
A facilitator may dispute whether this example represents local working arrangements; that uncertainty requires review.
risks: Restored access could be mistaken for permission to impose extra work.
A declined commitment could be interpreted as reluctance rather than unsupported capacity.
Practice could substitute for an accountable staffing or workflow decision.
system_capabilities: Represent access, authority and protected capacity separately; available access must not imply a feasible commitment.
On capacity withdrawal, invalidate pending review and display the changed dependency beside the current proposal.
Support a correctable inquiry or pause without assigning overtime, inferring consent or judging refusal.
tradeoffs: Reveal capacity details only for moves that require additional work.
Preserve original wording as history while qualifying the current proposal.

CURRENT ARTIFACTS: {"design":{"content":{"body":"## Problem and people

Conversation Lab proposes optional practice for first-time team leads using an invented missed-handoff story. A handoff note was absent on Monday, the next shift repeated a check, and the lead has not heard the colleague's account. The task is to distinguish observation from explanation, choose an opening, reconsider after additional context, and prepare a feasible conversation proposal. The missing note establishes neither carelessness nor responsibility for the repeated check; their causal relationship is unknown.

New leads, colleagues, managers, learning teams and employee representatives are prospective affected groups. None have participated. This integrated Design brief is a provisional synthesis for a rehearsal candidate, not approved requirements or demonstrated professional proficiency.

Sequence 2 is an actual preservation verification event. It preserves parent framing, Map and Design as background, including a hypothetical staffing interruption: tentative practice wording remains visible on a shared workstation and a supervisor associates it with capability. That interruption was not observed. The previous workforce journal remains an immutable parent, not a measured baseline or approved intervention. Sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13 supply specialist drafts rather than participant evidence.

Rival explanations for the workplace concern include changed schedules, inaccessible tools, unclear ownership, inadequate coverage and conflicting expectations. Conversation difficulty could be secondary to these conditions. Training is not the automatic response.

## Human and system capability

Human capability: participants need room to question observations, retain tentative interpretations, reject suggestions, withhold agreement, choose written participation, pass or stop without giving a reason. Leads must distinguish their own inquiry from changes requiring another person's authority. Managers must inspect staffing, protected time, workflow access, ownership and suitable space. Facilitators need covered time and must accommodate access needs without judging speech, confidence, speed, eye contact or script fidelity. No support owners, resources or participation protections are secured.

System capability: a deterministic browser activity will assemble explicitly authored fictional material and participant-selected proposals. It will not predict reactions, evaluate optional text, diagnose learning needs, infer consent or assess readiness. Keep supplied facts, tentative explanations, missing accounts, historical wording, current proposals and pending replacements distinct. Every proposed next move must carry relevant support, authority, unassigned work and unresolved agreement.

Use fictional inputs only. Exclude real employee records, identifiable recordings, profiling, ranking, consequential HR advice, automatic scores, telemetry, storage and network requests. Maintain only volatile state within the candidate frame; refresh or closure loses work. No export, sharing, certificate, attendance log, aid-use count or participant analytics is proposed. Humans retain all consequential workplace decisions and any separate decision to disclose material.

Language preferences, reading demands, devices, assistive technology, suitable space and coverage are unknown. Responsive layout, plain wording, visible focus and untimed keyboard operation are intended qualities to inspect, not established access. Recording nothing cannot prevent informal observation or employment pressure.

## Experience and decisions

The primary task is one conversation proposal, not a reflection questionnaire. Start with a compact situation board in linear reading order: Observed fictional facts, Possible explanations and Missing context. Show Monday's absent note and the repeated check as observations; show process, access or priority explanations as tentative; keep the unheard colleague account and uncertain causal relationship visible. Selecting an explanation never promotes it into a fact. Do not depend on dragging, color, hover or visual position.

Offer three openings with exact previews: “I noticed Monday's handoff note was absent. What was happening from your perspective?”; “Can we check how the handoff was meant to work on Monday?”; and “I need more context before deciding our next step.” The learner chooses an opening and a provisional next move through brief choices. Blank optional fields must still yield a useful initial proposal. Pass, Stop, Cover and Paper activity remain available without justification. Explain session loss before entry; keep detailed review metadata in Help.

Each opening changes an explicitly authored possible exchange and its descriptive implications. Provide possibilities in which the colleague offers context, questions an interpretation or requests a later discussion. Label these beside the dialogue as invented possibilities, not predictions or evidence about people. Participants may reject an example and continue with the account unresolved.

Capture the initial proposal, then reveal the supplied fictional context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague, and the expected owner was unclear. The reveal adds information without establishing a complete cause. Invite retaining or revising the interpretation and next move; neither receives praise, blame or a correctness label. Retained wording must still display the new constraints.

Offer next moves such as checking the current expectation, requesting support before proposing template use, or pausing until a suitable conversation is possible. Reveal relevant dependency choices only when needed. Unknown or unavailable support produces a conditional next move, a support inquiry or a pause, never an unconditional promise. Show whose authority would be needed without assigning an owner or repair work automatically. Even available fictional support leaves colleague agreement unresolved.

Preserve historical source facts. A later selection of available support means a hypothetical future condition for the proposed move; it must not rewrite Monday's inaccessible template or unclear owner. Label that distinction explicitly. The optional second situation has separate source data and must not inherit these facts.

Feedback describes what the selected wording states, whose account it invites and what remains unresolved. For a carelessness interpretation, distinguish the observed absence from its uncertain reason. For template use, name unresolved access and ownership. For a process inquiry, name the expectation being checked. For postponement, show that agreement is deferred and a suitable opportunity or support remains to be arranged. Feedback is contestable. Participants may reject it, retain a proposal or revise one component. An optional focused retry previews another authored possibility; it makes no claim that revision improves real conversations.

Show clearly labelled Initial proposal and Current proposal, including observation, invitation, next move, needed support, authority, unassigned work and unresolved questions or disagreement. State what changed or was retained neutrally. Keep “Fictional practice proposal; no workplace agreement or capability judgment” beside the output. A narrow layout may show versions sequentially while preserving their labels.

Use at most two optional main-path text fields: replacement wording and an unresolved question, both labelled for fictional content only. Correction shows the exact replacement, affected component and dependency summary before Apply or Cancel. Cancel preserves the current proposal. A relevant context or support change invalidates pending review and requires renewed inspection before Apply. Participant wording remains verbatim and labelled; the candidate cannot certify its feasibility. Support and agreement conditions remain independently visible even if entered wording contradicts them.

Cover immediately conceals all candidate content surfaces, including history, current plans, optional text, pending replacements, dialogue, second-situation content and open detail views. Concealed material must be unavailable through ordinary assistive-technology navigation. Move focus to a neutral screen. Explicit Resume restores the corrected state and offers optional orientation without requiring recall. No automatic resumption, inactivity scoring or interruption logs.

Finish and clear for handoff is separate from Cover. Review its scope and require confirmation; Cancel retains the session. Confirmation removes all candidate session values and rendered content, including both situations, selections, drafts, history and pending previews, then presents a neutral start state. Clearing must work from Cover without exposing content. Concealment retains volatile work; clearing removes candidate state. Neither prevents prior viewing, external capture or inspection beyond the candidate's control.

Offer one optional second fictional situation: “Two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check.” Begin with fewer suggestions, keeping help immediately available and recording no aid use. Use an opening and next move addressing disputed ownership; do not import the first situation's access barrier. Call this supported practice, never a transfer test or evidence of greater competence.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Inquiry, feedback and reciprocal agency. Origins: Workforce R1/R3 in sequence 5; Systems SE2 in sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD1/HCD2 in sequence 9; Learning scientist LS1–LS3 in sequence 11. Interaction: a labelled situation board, choice-specific authored previews, contestable descriptive feedback, fictional reveal, optional focused retry and correctable before/after proposal. Human reason: participants need to examine ambiguity and hear a missing perspective without conforming to a script. System reason: a polished preview can otherwise appear to diagnose the problem or predict a colleague. Acceptance: complete the task without typing, reject examples and feedback, retain a tentative interpretation after the reveal, and finish with unresolved disagreement or a pause; no score, agreement or readiness inference appears. Check the second situation retains only its supplied facts and remains supported practice. Task relevance, feedback criteria and access remain unreviewed.

R2 — Feasible support without delegated authority. Origins: Workforce R2 in sequence 5; Systems SE1 in sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD3 in sequence 9; Responsible AI RA1 in sequence 13. Interaction: choosing a dependent next move exposes support and authority, qualifies its wording and shows work still unassigned. Human reason: a lead cannot promise access repair, allocate another person's work or obtain agreement through a selection. System reason: dependency labels alone can coexist with an infeasible commitment. Acceptance: inaccessible template plus unclear ownership yields inquiry, a conditional proposal or pause; it never assigns repair or states unconditional use. Changing a prospective support condition leaves historical facts intact and requires renewed review of a pending replacement. Available support never implies colleague consent. Real resources and authority remain unknown.

R3 — Participant control, recovery and equivalent alternatives. Origins: the hypothetical interruption preserved by sequence 2; Workforce R4/R5 in sequence 5; Systems SE3/SE4 in sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD4/HCD5 in sequence 9; Learning scientist LS4 in sequence 11; Responsible AI RA2–RA4 in sequence 13. Interaction: exact Apply/Cancel, persistent Cover, explicit Resume with optional orientation, confirmed complete clearing and directly available paper materials. Human reason: interruption, dissent and device handoff require different voluntary decisions; recovery must not test memory. System reason: stale drafts, open Help and partial resets can expose or restore rejected content. Acceptance: apply one correction, cancel another, cover all surfaces by keyboard, resume the corrected state, cancel clearing, then confirm clearing from Cover and inspect a complete reset. Inspect focus, narrow layout, concealed accessibility content and absence of network, storage or tracking. Run the equivalent paper task without the browser. No checks have occurred; workplace privacy and credible refusal require human review.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Choices reduce writing burden but constrain expression; optional replacement and unresolved dissent preserve correction without requiring an essay. Examples support entry but can encourage imitation; rejecting them and requesting support remain legitimate. Support detail improves feasibility but adds work, so reveal it when the proposed move requires it. Before/after comparison makes revision visible without making revision the goal.

Retain dissent that workflow repair or no practice is preferable. Clarifying ownership, restoring accessible materials, inspecting the rota and arranging coverage are non-learning options requiring human authority. A deterministic browser activity is a non-AI option; facilitated paper practice is a complete alternative. Neither can secure participation protections or authorize organizational change.

Paper materials: situation card with the three initial story statements; board labelled Observed facts, Possible explanations and Missing context; the three exact opening cards above; blank replacement, Pass and Stop cards. Add a reveal card stating the changed rota, inaccessible template and unclear expected owner, labelled invented context rather than a complete explanation. Add authored response cards: “Here is additional context”, “I question that interpretation” and “I would prefer to discuss this later”; label them possibilities rather than predictions.

Provide Initial proposal and Current proposal sheets with spaces for observation, invitation, next move, support, authority, unassigned work and unresolved disagreement. Supply support cards Unknown, Unavailable and Available for the proposed fictional next move, a reminder that agreement remains unresolved, and a feedback card asking: “Which wording is observation or explanation?”, “Whose account or agreement is missing?” and “What support makes this move feasible?” Include a blank cover sheet and the exact second-situation card above; make opening suggestions available on request.

Facilitation: first arrange voluntary participation, protected time, accessible materials, suitable space and participant-controlled disposal. Present the situation and invite an opening or Pass; written selection is sufficient. Record the initial proposal, release the reveal, describe dependencies without grading and invite retaining or revising one component. Review the exact replacement before accepting it; cancellation keeps the current sheet. Leave disagreement and unassigned work visible. Offer a response-card retry, the second situation or stopping. Speech and role-play are optional. Do not solicit personal accounts, collect or photograph sheets, grade aid use, record attendance for assessment or require sharing. Cover for interruption and resume only by participant choice. Dispose of sheets under the agreed arrangement. These conditions have not been secured.

## Acceptance checks

Prepare fictional task walkthroughs for every opening, disputed interpretation, unavailable support, unclear authority, postponement and rejected feedback. Inspect concrete output with blank optional fields and faithful source distinctions. Compare retained and revised proposals without treating either as success.

Prepare recovery walkthroughs containing history, an applied correction, a cancelled replacement, a pending review, open Help and second-situation progress. Inspect renewed review after changed conditions, keyboard focus, concealment, accurate resumption and complete confirmed clearing. Separately inspect code and runtime for prohibited storage, network requests and tracking. These are planned checks, not observed behavior.

Practitioner, affected-person and representative review must separately examine comprehension, reciprocal dignity, language, device access, credible refusal, workload, privacy and paper handling. Technical verification establishes only the behavior inspected. It cannot establish free participation, learning, retention, transfer or flourishing.

## Evidence and unknowns

Actual references are sequence 2's preservation verification and Design drafts 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. The interruption is hypothetical; the seed supplies invented source material. No participant observations, consensus, human approval, technical results, field pilot or empirical success exist. Field evidence remains pending.

Changes after the interruption are complete participant-controlled concealment, correction-aware resumption without recall, and distinct confirmed handoff clearing. This synthesis additionally binds proposal wording to support, preserves workload and agreement boundaries, and distinguishes supported practice from transfer. These refine current Design; no named earlier requirement is invalidated, so Understand and Map remain preserved.

Unknowns include whether this is an important learning need, whether choices and feedback represent affected perspectives, whether refusal is credible and whether feasible support exists. Later apparent improvement could reflect copied examples, familiarity, facilitator cues, selective participation, repaired workflow or stronger managerial support. Difficulty could reflect reading, language, workload or dissent rather than a capability deficit. Delayed retention and adaptation to changed workplace conditions require separate reviewed evidence; they are outside this candidate's claims.

## Next decision

Proceed to a focused rehearsal Build implementing this brief with fictional data and deterministic interactions. Then perform the proposed technical walkthroughs and prepare practitioner and affected-person interaction review. Keep intended quality, observed technical behavior and untested learning, transfer and flourishing separate. Conversation Lab proposes optional practice for first-time team leads using an invented missed-handoff story. A handoff note was absent on Monday, the next shift repeated a check, and the lead has not heard the colleague's account. The task is to distinguish observation from explanation, choose an opening, reconsider after additional context, and prepare a feasible conversation proposal. The missing note establishes neither carelessness nor responsibility for the repeated check; their causal relationship is unknown.

New leads, colleagues, managers, learning teams and employee representatives are prospective affected groups. None have participated. This integrated Design brief is a provisional synthesis for a rehearsal candidate, not approved requirements or demonstrated professional proficiency.

Sequence 2 is an actual preservation verification event. It preserves parent framing, Map and Design as background, including a hypothetical staffing interruption: tentative practice wording remains visible on a shared workstation and a supervisor associates it with capability. That interruption was not observed. The previous workforce journal remains an immutable parent, not a measured baseline or approved intervention. Sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13 supply specialist drafts rather than participant evidence.

Rival explanations for the workplace concern include changed schedules, inaccessible tools, unclear ownership, inadequate coverage and conflicting expectations. Conversation difficulty could be secondary to these conditions. Training is not the automatic response.

## Human and system capability

Human capability: participants need room to question observations, retain tentative interpretations, reject suggestions, withhold agreement, choose written participation, pass or stop without giving a reason. Leads must distinguish their own inquiry from changes requiring another person's authority. Managers must inspect staffing, protected time, workflow access, ownership and suitable space. Facilitators need covered time and must accommodate access needs without judging speech, confidence, speed, eye contact or script fidelity. No support owners, resources or participation protections are secured.

System capability: a deterministic browser activity will assemble explicitly authored fictional material and participant-selected proposals. It will not predict reactions, evaluate optional text, diagnose learning needs, infer consent or assess readiness. Keep supplied facts, tentative explanations, missing accounts, historical wording, current proposals and pending replacements distinct. Every proposed next move must carry relevant support, authority, unassigned work and unresolved agreement.

Use fictional inputs only. Exclude real employee records, identifiable recordings, profiling, ranking, consequential HR advice, automatic scores, telemetry, storage and network requests. Maintain only volatile state within the candidate frame; refresh or closure loses work. No export, sharing, certificate, attendance log, aid-use count or participant analytics is proposed. Humans retain all consequential workplace decisions and any separate decision to disclose material.

Language preferences, reading demands, devices, assistive technology, suitable space and coverage are unknown. Responsive layout, plain wording, visible focus and untimed keyboard operation are intended qualities to inspect, not established access. Recording nothing cannot prevent informal observation or employment pressure.

## Experience and decisions

The primary task is one conversation proposal, not a reflection questionnaire. Start with a compact situation board in linear reading order: Observed fictional facts, Possible explanations and Missing context. Show Monday's absent note and the repeated check as observations; show process, access or priority explanations as tentative; keep the unheard colleague account and uncertain causal relationship visible. Selecting an explanation never promotes it into a fact. Do not depend on dragging, color, hover or visual position.

Offer three openings with exact previews: “I noticed Monday's handoff note was absent. What was happening from your perspective?”; “Can we check how the handoff was meant to work on Monday?”; and “I need more context before deciding our next step.” The learner chooses an opening and a provisional next move through brief choices. Blank optional fields must still yield a useful initial proposal. Pass, Stop, Cover and Paper activity remain available without justification. Explain session loss before entry; keep detailed review metadata in Help.

Each opening changes an explicitly authored possible exchange and its descriptive implications. Provide possibilities in which the colleague offers context, questions an interpretation or requests a later discussion. Label these beside the dialogue as invented possibilities, not predictions or evidence about people. Participants may reject an example and continue with the account unresolved.

Capture the initial proposal, then reveal the supplied fictional context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague, and the expected owner was unclear. The reveal adds information without establishing a complete cause. Invite retaining or revising the interpretation and next move; neither receives praise, blame or a correctness label. Retained wording must still display the new constraints.

Offer next moves such as checking the current expectation, requesting support before proposing template use, or pausing until a suitable conversation is possible. Reveal relevant dependency choices only when needed. Unknown or unavailable support produces a conditional next move, a support inquiry or a pause, never an unconditional promise. Show whose authority would be needed without assigning an owner or repair work automatically. Even available fictional support leaves colleague agreement unresolved.

Preserve historical source facts. A later selection of available support means a hypothetical future condition for the proposed move; it must not rewrite Monday's inaccessible template or unclear owner. Label that distinction explicitly. The optional second situation has separate source data and must not inherit these facts.

Feedback describes what the selected wording states, whose account it invites and what remains unresolved. For a carelessness interpretation, distinguish the observed absence from its uncertain reason. For template use, name unresolved access and ownership. For a process inquiry, name the expectation being checked. For postponement, show that agreement is deferred and a suitable opportunity or support remains to be arranged. Feedback is contestable. Participants may reject it, retain a proposal or revise one component. An optional focused retry previews another authored possibility; it makes no claim that revision improves real conversations.

Show clearly labelled Initial proposal and Current proposal, including observation, invitation, next move, needed support, authority, unassigned work and unresolved questions or disagreement. State what changed or was retained neutrally. Keep “Fictional practice proposal; no workplace agreement or capability judgment” beside the output. A narrow layout may show versions sequentially while preserving their labels.

Use at most two optional main-path text fields: replacement wording and an unresolved question, both labelled for fictional content only. Correction shows the exact replacement, affected component and dependency summary before Apply or Cancel. Cancel preserves the current proposal. A relevant context or support change invalidates pending review and requires renewed inspection before Apply. Participant wording remains verbatim and labelled; the candidate cannot certify its feasibility. Support and agreement conditions remain independently visible even if entered wording contradicts them.

Cover immediately conceals all candidate content surfaces, including history, current plans, optional text, pending replacements, dialogue, second-situation content and open detail views. Concealed material must be unavailable through ordinary assistive-technology navigation. Move focus to a neutral screen. Explicit Resume restores the corrected state and offers optional orientation without requiring recall. No automatic resumption, inactivity scoring or interruption logs.

Finish and clear for handoff is separate from Cover. Review its scope and require confirmation; Cancel retains the session. Confirmation removes all candidate session values and rendered content, including both situations, selections, drafts, history and pending previews, then presents a neutral start state. Clearing must work from Cover without exposing content. Concealment retains volatile work; clearing removes candidate state. Neither prevents prior viewing, external capture or inspection beyond the candidate's control.

Offer one optional second fictional situation: “Two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check.” Begin with fewer suggestions, keeping help immediately available and recording no aid use. Use an opening and next move addressing disputed ownership; do not import the first situation's access barrier. Call this supported practice, never a transfer test or evidence of greater competence.

R1 — Inquiry, feedback and reciprocal agency. Human reason: participants need to examine ambiguity and hear a missing perspective without conforming to a script. System reason: a polished preview can otherwise appear to diagnose the problem or predict a colleague. Acceptance: complete the task without typing, reject examples and feedback, retain a tentative interpretation after the reveal, and finish with unresolved disagreement or a pause; no score, agreement or readiness inference appears. R2 — Feasible support without delegated authority. Origins: Workforce R2 in sequence 5; Systems SE1 in sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD3 in sequence 9; Responsible AI RA1 in sequence 13. ## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Choices reduce writing burden but constrain expression; optional replacement and unresolved dissent preserve correction without requiring an essay. Examples support entry but can encourage imitation; rejecting them and requesting support remain legitimate. Support detail improves feasibility but adds work, so reveal it when the proposed move requires it. Before/after comparison makes revision visible without making revision the goal.

Retain dissent that workflow repair or no practice is preferable. Clarifying ownership, restoring accessible materials, inspecting the rota and arranging coverage are non-learning options requiring human authority. A deterministic browser activity is a non-AI option; facilitated paper practice is a complete alternative. Neither can secure participation protections or authorize organizational change.

Add a reveal card stating the changed rota, inaccessible template and unclear expected owner, labelled invented context rather than a complete explanation. Add authored response cards: “Here is additional context”, “I question that interpretation” and “I would prefer to discuss this later”; label them possibilities rather than predictions.
