Facilitation: first arrange voluntary participation, protected time, accessible materials, suitable space and participant-controlled disposal. Present the situation and invite an opening or Pass; written selection is sufficient. Record the initial proposal, release the reveal, describe dependencies without grading and invite retaining or revising one component. ## Problem and people

Conversation Lab proposes voluntary practice for first-time team leads using an invented missed-handoff story: a handoff note was absent on Monday, the next shift repeated a check, and the lead has not heard the colleague’s account. The task is to distinguish observation from explanation, choose an opening, reconsider changed information and prepare a feasible conversation proposal. The absent note establishes neither carelessness nor responsibility for the repeated check; their causal relationship remains unknown.

New leads, colleagues, managers, learning teams and employee representatives are prospective affected groups. None have participated. This is a revised rehearsal Design brief, not approved requirements or demonstrated proficiency. The previous workforce journal remains an immutable parent, not a measured baseline or approved intervention.

Sequence 15 integrates the specialist drafts at sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Sequence 2 preserves parent material, including a hypothetical shared-workstation interruption. Sequence 18 introduces another hypothetical event: after a template-dependent proposal exists, an authorized fictional manager offers restored access on the condition that the colleague completes the note after their shift; coverage and protected time have been withdrawn. The fictional colleague refuses the additional work. Ownership remains unresolved. Neither hypothetical event is an observation or prediction.

Rival explanations include changed schedules, inaccessible materials, unclear ownership, inadequate coverage and conflicting expectations. Conversation difficulty may be secondary to those conditions. Training is not the automatic response.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: participants need room to question observations, retain tentative interpretations, reject feedback, correct wording, withhold agreement, choose written participation, pass or stop without justification. Leads must distinguish inquiry from decisions requiring another person’s authority. A colleague’s refusal does not become a capability judgment. Managers must inspect protected time, coverage, access, ownership and suitable space. Authority to restore access does not establish authority to resolve every workflow condition or another person’s agreement. Facilitators need covered time and accessible materials; they must not grade speech, speed, confidence, eye contact or script fidelity. No resources, support owners or participation protections are secured.

System requirements: use deterministic choices and explicitly authored fictional examples. Separate source facts, possible explanations, missing accounts, initial history, current proposals and pending corrections. Represent access, relevant authority, protected capacity and agreement independently. Protected capacity comprises protected time and coverage; if either is unavailable, the combined condition is unavailable, and an unresolved component remains unknown. Do not use a single available-support label as a feasibility certificate.

Use fictional inputs only. Exclude real employee records, identifiable recordings, profiling, employee ranking, consequential HR advice, automatic scores, telemetry, storage and network requests. Keep only volatile state in the candidate frame; refresh or closure loses work. No export, sharing controls, certificates, attendance logs or aid-use records are proposed. Do not evaluate optional text or infer consent, readiness, reactions or learning needs. Humans retain consequential workplace decisions and any separate disclosure decision.

Language needs, reading demands, devices, assistive technology, suitable space and workflow resources are unknown. Responsive layout, plain wording, untimed keyboard use and visible focus are intended qualities requiring inspection. Recording nothing cannot prevent informal observation or employment pressure.

## Experience and decisions

The main task produces one conversation proposal through brief choices rather than a long questionnaire. Begin with a linear situation board labelled Observed fictional facts, Possible explanations and Missing context. Show the absent note and repeated check as observations; explanations remain tentative, including when selected. Keep the unheard colleague account and uncertain causal relationship visible. Do not rely on color, dragging, hover or spatial position.

Offer exact opening previews: “I noticed Monday’s handoff note was absent. What was happening from your perspective?”; “Can we check how the handoff was meant to work on Monday?”; and “I need more context before deciding our next step.” Choose an opening and provisional next move without mandatory typing. Pass, Stop, Cover and Paper activity remain available without reasons. Explain session loss before entry; place detailed review metadata in Help.

Each opening changes an explicitly authored possible exchange and descriptive feedback. Include a colleague offering context, questioning an interpretation or asking to discuss it later. Label dialogue beside the preview as invented possibilities, not predicted reactions or evidence about people. Participants can reject examples and feedback, retain their proposal or retry an opening against another authored possibility. No branch receives praise, blame, scores or a preferred-answer marker.

Capture the Initial proposal before revealing the supplied context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague, and the expected owner was unclear. This adds information without proving a complete cause. Invite retaining or revising the interpretation and next move. Retaining wording must still display the new constraints.

For a next move involving template use or additional handoff work, reveal relevant dependency choices: access, authority to resolve the proposed condition, and protected time/coverage, each Available, Unavailable or Unknown within the fictional prospective situation. Show what authority is needed and what work remains unassigned. Offer checking expectations, requesting support or pausing. Unknown or unavailable conditions produce a conditional proposal, inquiry or pause; they never produce an unconditional commitment. Even available support leaves reciprocal agreement unresolved.

Introduce sequence 18’s changed-condition card after a template-dependent initial proposal exists. A pending correction may remain open when the participant activates the card so the recovery rule is inspectable. Display: “Access offered; protected capacity unavailable; colleague agreement withheld; ownership unresolved.” Display the authored response: “Making the template accessible does not give me time to complete it after my shift. I cannot agree to that extra work.” Label the event and response hypothetical. An offer to restore access is distinct from confirmed availability, and neither supplies time or agreement.

After that event, offer three concrete routes: request clarification of protected capacity and ownership; reconsider the next move; or pause. Authored synthesis must leave additional work unassigned and avoid promising after-shift completion. Retaining wording or rejecting feedback remains possible, with the conflict independently visible. Prospective support changes must not erase the recorded refusal or invent later agreement. They must also leave Monday’s inaccessible template, unclear owner and the withdrawal event intact as fictional history.

Show clearly labelled Initial proposal and Current proposal. Each contains observation, invitation, next move, relevant support, authority, protected capacity, unassigned work and unresolved questions or disagreement. State neutrally what changed or was retained. Put “Fictional practice proposal; no workplace agreement or capability judgment” beside the output. On narrow screens, versions may appear sequentially with explicit labels.

Feedback describes what wording states, whose account it invites and what remains unresolved. A carelessness interpretation remains an explanation rather than an observed cause. A process inquiry identifies the expectation being checked. Template use names access, ownership and capacity conditions. Pausing leaves a suitable opportunity and agreement unarranged. Feedback is contestable; revising is not itself success.

Use at most two optional main-path text fields: replacement wording and an unresolved question, both for fictional content only. A component selector identifies what the replacement changes. Review shows the exact replacement, affected component and dependency summary before Apply or Cancel. Cancel preserves the current proposal. Applied participant wording remains verbatim and labelled; the candidate cannot certify its feasibility. Independent conditions remain visible even if the text contradicts them.

A relevant context or support change, including sequence 18’s event, invalidates any pending correction review. Preserve the draft, mark the review stale and disable Apply until the participant explicitly reviews the exact replacement with the updated conditions. Renewed review enables a separate Apply decision; reviewing alone does not apply it. Cancel preserves current wording and the newly revealed conditions rather than reversing the event.

Cover immediately conceals all content surfaces, including scenario, history, current plans, text fields, pending reviews, dialogue, second-situation progress and open detail views. Concealed content must be unavailable through ordinary assistive-technology navigation. Move focus to a neutral screen. Resume is explicit, restores current corrections and the capacity conflict, and offers optional orientation without a recall task. Stale reviews remain stale. No automatic resumption, interruption logs or inactivity assessment.

Finish and clear for handoff is separate from Cover. Describe the scope and require confirmation; Cancel retains the session. Confirmation resets every candidate value and rendered surface, including both situations, initial/current plans, support and capacity choices, refusal state, drafts and pending previews, then shows a neutral start screen. Clearing must work from Cover without revealing content. Cover retains volatile work; clearing removes candidate session state. Neither prevents prior viewing or external capture.

Offer one optional second situation: “Two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check.” Begin with fewer suggestions and keep help immediately available without recording its use. Produce an ownership-focused opening and next move through choices. Keep its source data and state separate: do not inherit Monday’s access barrier or sequence 18’s refusal and capacity withdrawal. Call it supported practice, not a transfer test.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Inquiry and reciprocal agency. Origins: Workforce R1/R3, sequence 5; Systems SE2, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD1/HCD2, sequence 9; Learning scientist LS1–LS3, sequence 11; integrated in sequence 15. Interaction: labelled board, distinct opening previews, contestable feedback, context reveal, optional retry and before/after proposal. Human reason: participants need to examine ambiguity without conforming to a script or losing dissent. System reason: polished examples can imply diagnosis or predicted reactions. Check: complete without typing, exercise every opening, reject examples and feedback, retain a tentative interpretation and finish with unresolved disagreement or a pause. Inspect separate second-situation facts and available support. Relevance, language and feedback criteria remain unreviewed.

R2 — Separate feasibility conditions and agreement. Origins: Workforce R2, sequence 5; Systems SE1, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD3, sequence 9; Responsible AI RA1, sequence 13; sequence 15 R2; Scenario SC1, sequence 18. Interaction: distinguish access, authority, protected capacity and agreement; introduce capacity withdrawal after an initial proposal; offer clarification, reconsideration or pause. Human reason: usable tools and managerial authority do not supply time, coverage or consent. System reason: an available-support selection can otherwise conceal an unsupported commitment. Check: available access plus unavailable capacity and withheld agreement yields qualified wording, unassigned work and unresolved ownership, without after-shift promises. Prospective support changes preserve source history and refusal. Actual resources, authority and workload arrangements remain unknown.

R3 — Correction, recovery and equivalent alternatives. Origins: hypothetical interruption preserved at sequence 2; Workforce R4/R5, sequence 5; Systems SE3/SE4, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD4/HCD5, sequence 9; Learning scientist LS4, sequence 11; Responsible AI RA2–RA4, sequence 13; sequence 15 R3; Scenario SC1, sequence 18. Interaction: exact review/Apply/Cancel, stale-review handling, complete Cover, explicit Resume, confirmed handoff clearing and direct paper access. Human reason: interruption and dissent require control without memory tests or loss of refusal. System reason: stale previews and partial resets can expose or restore rejected content. Check: introduce withdrawal during review, require renewed inspection, cancel without reversing the event, cover/resume the corrected state and confirm complete clearing from Cover. Inspect keyboard focus, concealment, narrow layout and prohibited technical behavior. Run the full paper task. No checks have occurred.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Choices reduce entry burden but constrain expression; optional correction and unresolved questions preserve another route. Examples support participation but can invite imitation; rejecting them and requesting help remain legitimate. Dependency details add work, so reveal them when the next move requires them. Before/after comparison makes revision inspectable without rewarding change.

Retain dissent that organizational repair or no practice is preferable. An accountable review of rota, coverage, protected time, ownership and accessible materials is a non-learning option. The candidate cannot authorize repairs. Deterministic browser practice and facilitated paper practice are non-AI options; neither secures participation protections.

Complete paper materials: a situation card containing the three initial story statements; a board labelled Observed facts, Possible explanations and Missing context; the three exact opening cards above; blank replacement, Pass and Stop cards. A reveal card states the changed rota, inaccessible template and unclear owner, labelled invented context rather than a complete cause. Authored response cards say “Here is additional context”, “I question that interpretation” and “I would prefer to discuss this later”, labelled possibilities rather than predictions.

Provide Initial proposal and Current proposal sheets with spaces for observation, invitation, next move, access, authority, protected time/coverage, agreement, unassigned work and unresolved questions. Supply Available, Unavailable and Unknown cards for support conditions; agreement remains separately unresolved or withheld. Add sequence 18’s complete changed-condition card and exact refusal above. Add a feedback card asking: “Which wording is observation or explanation?”, “Whose account or agreement is missing?” and “What support makes the move feasible?” Include a blank cover sheet and the exact second-situation card, with opening suggestions available on request.

Facilitation: arrange voluntary participation, protected time, accessible materials, suitable space and participant-controlled disposal first. Present the situation, invite an opening or Pass, and record the initial proposal. Release the reveal; for a template-dependent proposal, release the changed-condition card after the initial plan exists. Preserve refusal and leave additional work unassigned. Invite retention, one-component revision or stopping; describe implications without grading. Show the exact replacement and conditions before accepting it; cancellation preserves the current sheet. If conditions change during review, review again before acceptance. Offer an optional response-card retry or the separate second situation. Written selection is sufficient; speech and role-play are optional. Cover for interruption and resume only by participant choice. Do not solicit personal accounts, collect or photograph sheets, grade aid use, record attendance for assessment or require sharing. Dispose under the participant-controlled arrangement. These conditions are not secured.

## Acceptance checks

Plan fictional task walkthroughs for all openings, retained interpretations, rejected feedback, inaccessible templates, disputed ownership and postponed discussion. Complete with blank optional fields. Inspect faithful source distinctions, useful output and absence of scores or implied agreement.

Plan a capacity and recovery walkthrough: preserve an initial template proposal, open correction review, reveal sequence 18’s event, inspect stale-review handling and qualified output, renew review, cancel, cover and resume. Inspect preserved refusal and current wording; cancel clearing once, then confirm from Cover and inspect both situations and all state reset. Separately inspect keyboard behavior, concealed accessibility content, responsive layout, code and runtime for storage, tracking and network requests. These are planned checks, not observed behavior.

Pending practitioner, affected-person and representative review must examine comprehension, credible refusal, reciprocal dignity, belonging, language, device access, sustainable workload, screen visibility and paper handling. Technical verification would establish only inspected behavior, not free participation, learning, retention, transfer or flourishing.

## Evidence and unknowns

Sequence 15 supplies the previous integrated Design and its specialist origins; sequence 18 supplies the hypothetical capacity conflict. Neither is empirical evidence. Sequence 2’s preservation event does not approve the preserved material. No participant observations, consensus, human approval, technical results, field pilot or empirical success exists. Field evidence remains pending.

The concrete change from sequence 15 is independent protected-capacity representation, an actionable withdrawal/refusal state, renewed correction review and complete recovery coverage of those values. Preserve its inquiry, access, authority, disagreement and paper requirements. Design is the earliest supplied interaction artifact invalidated by this event; the material does not establish an omission in Map.

Unknowns include task relevance, local shift arrangements, authority to secure protected time, credible refusal, acceptable feedback and added burden. Apparent improvement could reflect copied examples, familiarity, facilitator cues, selective participation or repaired workflow. Difficulty could reflect language, reading demands, workload or dissent rather than a capability deficit. Immediate supported performance, delayed retention and adaptation in changed workplace conditions require different evidence; none is established here.

## Next decision

Replace sequence 15’s Design brief with this targeted revision, then implement a focused deterministic rehearsal Build. Exercise the planned fictional technical cases and prepare practitioner and affected-person interaction review. Keep intended quality, subsequently observed technical behavior and untested learning and flourishing separate. This is one Design revision, with no request to reopen Map. Any later field-use decision requires accountable human review of participation, capacity, access, authority and privacy; no launch authority exists.

Sequence 15 supplies the previous integrated Design and its specialist origins; sequence 18 supplies the hypothetical capacity conflict. Neither is empirical evidence. Sequence 2’s preservation event does not approve the preserved material. No participant observations, consensus, human approval, technical results, field pilot or empirical success exists. <body>
<div id="app"></div>
<script>
'use strict';
const app = document.getElementById('app');
const openingTexts = {
 inquiry:'I noticed Monday’s handoff note was absent. What was happening from your perspective?',
 process:'Can we check how the handoff was meant to work on Monday?',
 wait:'I need more context before deciding our next step.'
};
const interpretations = {
 unknown:'I do not yet have an explanation.',
 workflow:'The workflow may have made the note difficult to complete.',
 missed:'The note may have been overlooked.',
 careless:'Carelessness is one possible explanation; it is not an observed cause.'
};
const nextNames = {template:'Explore a shared template step',clarify:'Check expectations and ownership',pause:'Pause until a suitable opportunity'};
const supportNames = {access:'Template access',authority:'Relevant authority',time:'Protected time',coverage:'Shift coverage'};
const componentNames = {observation:'Observation',invitation:'Invitation',next:'Next move'};
function freshSession(){return {opening:'inquiry',interpretation:'unknown',next:'template',response:'context',rejected:false,initial:null,revealed:false,withdrawn:false,routeChoice:'',accessOffered:false,support:{access:'unknown',authority:'unknown',time:'unknown',coverage:'unknown'},overrides:{},question:'',draft:{component:'invitation',replacement:'',question:''},review:null,conditionVersion:0,second:{started:false,opening:'account',next:'map',applied:false}};}
function freshUI(){return {view:'start',returnTo:'start',coverReturn:'start',clearReturn:'start',stopReturn:'main',stopKind:'stop',orientation:false,status:''};}
let session = freshSession();
let ui = freshUI();
function esc(value){return String(value ?? '').replace(/[&<>"']/g,c=>({'&':'&','<':'<','>':'>','"':'"',"'":'''}[c]));}
function button(action,label,kind='',extra=''){return `<button type="button" data-action="${action}" ${extra} class="${kind}">${label}</button>`;}
function capacity(support){if(support.time==='unavailable'||support.coverage==='unavailable')return 'unavailable';if(support.time==='available'&&support.coverage==='available')return 'available';return 'unknown';}
function snapshot(){return {opening:session.opening,interpretation:session.interpretation,next:session.next,support:{...session.support},overrides:{...session.overrides},question:session.question,revealed:session.revealed,withdrawn:session.withdrawn,accessOffered:session.accessOffered,routeChoice:session.routeChoice};}
function agreement(p){return p.withdrawn?'withheld for the additional work; no later agreement supplied':'unresolved; the colleague has not agreed';}
function authoredNext(p){
 if(p.next==='pause')return 'Pause the proposal. Ask whether a suitable time and format can be arranged; no meeting or work is assigned.';
 if(p.next==='clarify')return p.withdrawn?'Request clarification of ownership, protected time and coverage. Leave additional work unassigned; the recorded refusal remains.':'Ask how the handoff was meant to work and who is expected to own each step. Request clarification before assigning work.';
 if(p.withdrawn)return 'Ask the appropriate workflow owner to clarify protected time, coverage and ownership before discussing a template step. Leave additional work unassigned; do not promise after-shift completion.';
 return 'Explore a template step only if access, relevant authority, protected time, coverage and reciprocal agreement can be established. Leave the work unassigned until those conditions are resolved.';
}
function authoredObservation(p){return 'Monday’s handoff note was absent. The next shift repeated a check. The causal relationship between these observations is unknown.';}
function authoredInvitation(p){return openingTexts[p.opening];}
function valueFor(p,key){if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(p.overrides,key))return p.overrides[key];return key==='observation'?authoredObservation(p):key==='invitation'?authoredInvitation(p):authoredNext(p);}
function unresolved(p){let out=['The colleague’s full account and the repeated check’s cause remain unknown.','Expected ownership and agreement remain unresolved.'];if(p.next==='template'||p.withdrawn)out.push('Who can secure access, protected time and coverage, and authorize the proposed work?');if(p.withdrawn)out.push('The colleague refused additional after-shift work. No later agreement is supplied.');if(p.question)out.push('Participant question (verbatim): '+p.question);return out;}
function supportSummary(p){return `<div class="summary"><span>Access: ${esc(p.support.access)}${p.accessOffered?' · offer recorded':''}</span><span>Authority: ${esc(p.support.authority)}</span><span class="${capacity(p.support)==='unavailable'?'conflict':''}">Protected capacity: ${capacity(p.support)}</span><span class="${p.withdrawn?'conflict':''}">Agreement: ${p.withdrawn?'withheld':'unresolved'}</span></div>`;}
function plan(p,label){return `<article class="panel plan"><p class="version">${label}</p><h3>${p.next==='template'?'A conditional template proposal':p.next==='clarify'?'An inquiry into ownership':'A pause proposal'}</h3><p class="fiction">Fictional practice proposal</p><p class="small muted">No workplace agreement or capability judgment.</p><dl><dt>Observation ${p.overrides.observation!==undefined?'· participant wording':''}</dt><dd>${esc(valueFor(p,'observation'))}</dd><dt>Invitation ${p.overrides.invitation!==undefined?'· participant wording':''}</dt><dd>${esc(valueFor(p,'invitation'))}</dd><dt>Tentative interpretation</dt><dd>${esc(interpretations[p.interpretation])} Selecting it does not establish a cause.</dd><dt>Next move ${p.overrides.next!==undefined?'· participant wording':''}</dt><dd>${esc(valueFor(p,'next'))}</dd><dt>Independent feasibility conditions</dt><dd>${supportSummary(p)}<span class="small">Time: ${esc(p.support.time)}. Coverage: ${esc(p.support.coverage)}. Relevant authority means authority to clarify ownership and arrange the proposed support; its scope still needs checking.</span></dd><dt>Agreement and unassigned work</dt><dd>Agreement is ${esc(agreement(p))}. Additional handoff work remains unassigned.${p.accessOffered?' Restored access has been offered, not confirmed.':''}</dd><dt>Unresolved questions / disagreement</dt><dd>${unresolved(p).map(x=>`<p class="small">${esc(x)}</p>`).join('')}</dd></dl>${Object.keys(p.overrides).length?'<p class="notice">Participant wording is displayed verbatim. The candidate cannot certify its feasibility; independent conditions above still apply.</p>':''}<p class="authored">${p.revealed?'Reveal retained: rota changed; Monday’s template inaccessible; expected owner unclear.':'The colleague’s account has not been heard.'}${p.withdrawn?' History retained: capacity withdrawn and agreement withheld.':''}</p></article>`;}
function nav(){return `<header class="top"><div class="brand">Conversation<span> / </span>Lab</div><nav class="nav" aria-label="Session controls">${button('pass','Pass')}${button('stop','Stop')}${button('cover','Cover')}${button('paper','Paper activity')}${button('help','Help')}${button('clear','Finish & clear')}</nav></header>`;}
function shell(body,withNav=true){return `<a class="skip" href="#content">Skip to content</a><div class="wrap">${withNav?nav():`<header class="top"><div class="brand">Conversation<span> / </span>Lab</div><span class="fiction">Fictional rehearsal</span></header>`}<main id="content" tabindex="-1">${body}</main><footer class="footer">Voluntary fictional practice · No scores or recordings · Work lasts only in this open page. Refreshing or closing loses it.</footer></div>`;}
function scene(){return `<div class="scene"><svg viewBox="0 0 470 215" role="img" aria-labelledby="scene-title scene-desc"><title id="scene-title">Two observed events, an unheard account</title><desc id="scene-desc">Monday: handoff note absent. Next shift: a check repeated. A colleague’s account is missing. Timeline order does not establish causation.</desc><path d="M50 108H414" stroke="#659f9b" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 6"/><rect x="20" y="35" width="132" height="142" rx="14" fill="#e9f3ee"/><rect x="169" y="35" width="132" height="142" rx="14" fill="#e9f3ee"/><rect x="318" y="35" width="132" height="142" rx="14" fill="#264b58" stroke="#91bcb7"/><g fill="#173640" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="13"><text x="35" y="60" font-weight="700">MONDAY</text><text x="184" y="60" font-weight="700">NEXT SHIFT</text><text x="35" y="141">Handoff note</text><text x="35" y="159" font-weight="700">absent</text><text x="184" y="141">Check</text><text x="184" y="159" font-weight="700">repeated</text></g><path d="M62 76h38v42H62zM69 88h24M69 98h17" stroke="#176b66" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><circle cx="232" cy="96" r="20" fill="none" stroke="#176b66" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M222 96l7 7 14-16" fill="none" stroke="#176b66" stroke-width="3"/><g fill="#e9f3ee" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="13"><text x="333" y="60" font-weight="700">STILL MISSING</text><text x="333" y="141">Colleague’s</text><text x="333" y="159" font-weight="700">account</text><text x="372" y="112" text-anchor="middle" font-size="36">?</text></g><text x="235" y="205" fill="#d0e4e4" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif">Sequence is visible. Cause is not established.</text></svg><p>Invented situation. No employee records or evidence about real people.</p></div>`;}
function startPage(){return `<section class="hero"><div><p class="eyebrow">First-time team lead practice</p><h1>A missing note.<br>An unheard account.</h1><p>Your mission: prepare an observation, an invitation and a feasible shared next move. Inspect what changes when workflow support and agreement are missing.</p><p class="fiction">Invented missed-handoff story</p><div class="actions">${button('begin','Begin with the situation','primary')}${button('paper','Use the paper activity')}${button('help','Review Help')}</div><p class="small muted" style="margin-top:16px">Choices are ready to inspect. Writing and speaking are optional. You may pass or stop without a reason.</p></div>${scene()}</section><div class="two"><section class="panel"><h2>Your choices remain yours</h2><p>Keep or revise, reject examples, leave questions unresolved or pause. No person is evaluated.</p></section><section class="panel"><h2>Before you begin</h2><p>Use fictional content only. Work stays in this page’s volatile memory; refresh or closure loses it. Cover conceals and retains work. Finish & clear removes the candidate’s session after confirmation.</p><p class="small muted">Arrange participation, space and protected time with accountable humans. None are secured here.</p></section></div>`;}
function board(){return `<section class="board" aria-label="Situation board"><div class="section-head"><h2>Separate the story from the explanation</h2><span class="fiction">Fictional source facts</span></div><div class="grid"><article class="panel"><span class="tag">Observed facts</span><ul><li>Monday’s handoff note was absent.</li><li>The next shift repeated a check.</li></ul><p class="small muted" style="margin-top:14px">These observations do not prove that the absent note caused the repeated check.</p></article><article class="panel"><span class="tag">Possible explanations</span><ul><li>A changed rota or conflicting expectations.</li><li>Unavailable materials or unclear ownership.</li><li>A missed note or other context.</li></ul><p class="small muted" style="margin-top:14px">Each remains tentative, including your selection.</p></article><article class="panel"><span class="tag amber">Missing context</span><ul><li>The colleague’s complete account.</li><li>What caused the repeated check.</li><li>Who owned the note and what support existed.</li></ul></article></div></section>`;}
function radio(name,value,title,description,current){return `<label class="choice"><input type="radio" name="${name}" value="${value}" data-focus="${name}-${value}" ${current===value?'checked':''}><span><b>${title}</b><small>${description}</small></span></label>`;}
function openingSection(){return `<section class="panel"><h2>Choose an opening</h2><p class="muted">Each opens a different authored possibility. Try another, or reject the example; none predicts a real colleague’s response.</p><fieldset><legend>Exact opening previews</legend><div class="choice-grid">${radio('opening','inquiry','Start with an observation',esc(openingTexts.inquiry),session.opening)}${radio('opening','process','Ask about the process',esc(openingTexts.process),session.opening)}${radio('opening','wait','Hold the decision',esc(openingTexts.wait),session.opening)}</div></fieldset>${dialogue()}</section>`;}
function dialogue(){const lines={inquiry:{context:'“I can share what I understood the handoff to involve.”',question:'“Are you assuming the missing note caused the repeated check?”',later:'“I would prefer to discuss this later.”'},process:{context:'“The instructions I saw did not make the owner clear.”',question:'“Which expectation are we checking, and who set it?”',later:'“Can we choose a different time to go through the process?”'},wait:{context:'“I have context to add before we decide anything.”',question:'“What information would you need before making that decision?”',later:'“I would prefer to leave this conversation for now.”'}};
 const feedback={inquiry:'This wording names the absent note and asks for the colleague’s perspective. It does not establish who was responsible or what caused the repeated check.',process:'This wording puts the expected process under examination. The relevant expectation, its owner and the colleague’s account are still missing.',wait:'This wording postpones a decision. It does not arrange a suitable opportunity or secure the colleague’s agreement.'};
 return `<div class="toolbar"><label for="response" class="small">Try a possible response</label><select id="response" data-focus="response" name="response"><option value="context" ${session.response==='context'?'selected':''}>Offers context</option><option value="question" ${session.response==='question'?'selected':''}>Questions the interpretation</option><option value="later" ${session.response==='later'?'selected':''}>Asks to discuss it later</option></select></div><div class="dialogue"><span class="fiction">Authored fictional possibility · not a prediction</span><p class="small" style="margin-top:12px"><b>Lead opening:</b> ${esc(openingTexts[session.opening])}</p><blockquote>${esc(lines[session.opening][session.response])}</blockquote><cite>Invented colleague response</cite><p class="small" style="margin-top:14px"><b>Descriptive feedback:</b> ${esc(feedback[session.opening])}</p></div>${button('reject',session.rejected?'Use the example again':'Reject this example / feedback')} ${session.rejected?'<p class="notice">Example and feedback rejected. Your proposal and choices remain available; rejection has no score or capability meaning.</p>':''}`;
}
function planningChoices(){return `<section class="panel"><h2>${session.initial?'Retain or reconsider':'Make a provisional plan'}</h2><p class="muted">Starter choices are editable. Change is not a success signal.</p><fieldset><legend>Tentative interpretation</legend><div class="line-choice">${radio('interpretation','unknown','No explanation yet','Keep the cause unresolved.',session.interpretation)}${radio('interpretation','workflow','Workflow may be involved','An explanation to examine, not a finding.',session.interpretation)}${radio('interpretation','missed','The note may have been overlooked','Responsibility and cause remain unknown.',session.interpretation)}${radio('interpretation','careless','Carelessness is possible','A tentative interpretation, never an observed cause.',session.interpretation)}</div></fieldset><fieldset><legend>Provisional next move</legend><div class="choice-grid">${radio('next','template',nextNames.template,'Conditional on access, authority, protected capacity and agreement.',session.next)}${radio('next','clarify',nextNames.clarify,'Ask what was expected and who can resolve it.',session.next)}${radio('next','pause',nextNames.pause,'Leave the proposal unassigned and a suitable opportunity unarranged.',session.next)}</div></fieldset>${session.overrides.next!==undefined?'<p class="notice">The next-move choice supplies descriptive context. Your applied replacement wording remains verbatim until you explicitly replace or restore it.</p>':''}${!session.initial?`<div class="actions">${button('capture','Record the initial proposal','primary')}</div><p class="small muted" style="margin-top:12px">Capture this version before new fictional context is revealed. No agreement is recorded.</p>`:''}</section>`;}
function contextSection(){if(!session.initial)return '';if(!session.revealed)return `<section class="panel tint"><h2>Your initial proposal is recorded</h2><p>Keep this before version visible. The next card adds fictional context; it does not prove a complete cause.</p>${button('reveal','Reveal the additional context','primary')}</section>`;return `<section class="panel tint"><div class="section-head"><h2>New context, still an incomplete account</h2><span class="fiction">Supplied fictional reveal</span></div><div class="grid"><p><b>The rota changed.</b><br>The schedule was different.</p><p><b>The template was inaccessible.</b><br>The colleague could not access it on Monday.</p><p><b>The expected owner was unclear.</b><br>Responsibility was unresolved.</p></div><p class="small">Retain or revise. Added context proves neither cause nor agreement.</p></section>`;}
function supportControls(){if(!session.revealed||!(session.next==='template'||session.withdrawn))return '';return `<section class="panel"><h2>What would this move depend on?</h2><p>Inspect each condition separately. These choices are <b>fictional prospective assumptions</b>, not verified resources. Available access alone cannot make a plan feasible.</p><div class="support">${Object.keys(supportNames).map(k=>`<label for="support-${k}">${supportNames[k]}<select id="support-${k}" name="support-${k}" data-focus="support-${k}">${['unknown','available','unavailable'].map(v=>`<option value="${v}" ${session.support[k]===v?'selected':''}>${v[0].toUpperCase()+v.slice(1)}</option>`).join('')}</select><small>${k==='authority'?'Who can clarify ownership and arrange this support? Scope still needs checking.':k==='access'?'An offer is distinct from confirmed availability.':k==='time'?'Time within an agreed, protected arrangement.':'Someone must cover the shift work.'}</small></label>`).join('')}</div>${supportSummary(snapshot())}<p class="small">Capacity: unavailable if either component is unavailable; unknown if one is unknown. Agreement stays separate.</p>${session.withdrawn?'<p class="notice conflict">Prospective changes preserve Monday’s barrier, withdrawal and refusal. Work is unassigned; no later agreement is supplied.</p>':''}</section>`;}
function withdrawalCard(){if(!session.revealed)return '';if(!session.initial||session.initial.next!=='template')return `<section class="panel"><h2>Changed-condition card</h2><p class="small muted">This card requires a template initial plan. Yours uses another route; finish it or confirm clearing to try a fresh template plan.</p></section>`;if(!session.withdrawn)return `<section class="panel warning"><span class="fiction">Hypothetical changed condition</span><h2>Test the support beneath your plan</h2><p>A fictional manager is about to offer access on a condition. You can reveal this card while an exact correction review is pending, to inspect how new conditions affect it.</p>${button('withdraw','Reveal the manager’s condition','primary')}</section>`;return `<section class="panel warning"><span class="fiction">Hypothetical event and authored response · not a prediction</span><h2>Access is offered. Capacity is withdrawn.</h2><p>An authorized fictional manager offers restored access <b>if the colleague completes the note after their shift</b>. Protected time and coverage have been withdrawn. Ownership remains unresolved.</p><p class="notice conflict"><b>Access offered; protected capacity unavailable; colleague agreement withheld; ownership unresolved.</b><br>This is the recorded event. Later prospective choices do not erase it.</p><div class="dialogue"><cite>Authored fictional refusal</cite><blockquote>“Making the template accessible does not give me time to complete it after my shift. I cannot agree to that extra work.”</blockquote></div><p>The offer does not confirm access, supply protected capacity or establish agreement. Additional work stays unassigned.</p><div class="actions">${button('route-clarify','Request capacity & ownership clarification')}${button('route-reconsider','Reconsider the next move')}${button('route-pause','Pause')}</div>${session.routeChoice?`<p class="notice">${session.routeChoice==='clarify'?'Clarification route selected. No support or agreement is assumed.':session.routeChoice==='reconsider'?'Reconsideration selected. function correctionSection(){if(!session.initial)return '';const r=session.review;return `<section class="panel edit"><h2>Correct one component, then review</h2><p>Optional fictional content. ## Problem and people
The supplied candidate addresses Design revision 2, sequence 20: voluntary first-time-lead practice using the invented missed-handoff story. No affected people participated. Sequence 2 preserves parent records, including Map, but their complete contents are not supplied here; Map conformity cannot be independently established.

## Human and system capability
Humans retain participation, disclosure, agreement and workplace decisions. Resources and authority remain unsecured. The source uses deterministic fictional choices and volatile session state. It separates access, relevant authority, protected time, coverage and agreement; it does not evaluate optional wording.

## Experience and decisions
Source reading identifies a labelled situation board, three exact openings, authored response alternatives, initial capture, context reveal and current synthesis. A template initial proposal unlocks sequence 18’s hypothetical access offer, capacity withdrawal and refusal. Clarification, reconsideration and pause leave additional work unassigned. Separate supported practice uses the second ownership story without inheriting Monday’s conflict.

## Requirements and rationale
R1, sequence 20’s Workforce, Human-centered designer and Learning scientist synthesis: choices, contestable examples and before/after output make inquiry and revision inspectable without grading. Check every opening, retained interpretation, rejected feedback and blank-field completion.
R2, sequence 20’s Systems and Responsible AI synthesis, revised after sequence 18: independent support conditions and withheld agreement qualify the proposal. Check that prospective available support never erases refusal or assigns after-shift work.
R3, sequence 20’s recovery requirement: exact review/Apply/Cancel, stale-review blocking, Cover/Resume and confirmed clearing appear in the source. However, shell() emits an href fragment link, contrary to the explicit no-links constraint. Replace it with a button that focuses main content, preserving keyboard access. Check activation and focus placement in the browser.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives
Defaults reduce entry burden but can imply preferred choices; correction and rejection remain available. Dependency details expose workload conditions while increasing reading. The complete paper route supplies story, board, openings, responses, reveal, support cards, withdrawal/refusal, two proposal sheets, correction, second situation, facilitation and disposal instructions. Workflow repair and no practice remain legitimate alternatives.

## Acceptance checks
Pending browser checks: choice-specific output, complete initial/current comparison, stale review after withdrawal, renewed review followed by separate Apply, and cancellation preserving new conditions. Inspect Cover concealment and explicit recovery, cancel clearing, then confirm clearing from Cover across both situations. Inspect keyboard focus, responsive layout, assistive-technology access and absence of storage, requests and telemetry. These checks have not occurred.

## Evidence and unknowns
Sequence 27 reports recovery of unchanged candidate.html with SHA-256 28b49bae6426cfde9945ee68c5c464aa70454612d70428adcda53969a2ca10ce and a passed independent node syntax check. It supplies no completed browser report. This receipt reviews supplied source; it does not establish runtime behavior. Practitioner and affected-person review remain pending. Rival explanations include workflow barriers; apparent improvement could reflect imitation, familiarity or facilitator cues. Learning, retention, transfer, free participation and flourishing remain untested; field evidence is pending.

## Next decision
Request one bounded Build revision to remove the link while preserving accessible navigation, then submit the candidate for scoped technical and human interaction review. Retain Design revision 2. No field release or human approval is granted.

CURRENT ARTIFACTS: {"design":{"content":{"body":"## Problem and people

Conversation Lab proposes voluntary practice for first-time team leads using an invented missed-handoff story: a handoff note was absent on Monday, the next shift repeated a check, and the lead has not heard the colleague’s account. The task is to distinguish observation from explanation, choose an opening, reconsider changed information and prepare a feasible conversation proposal. The absent note establishes neither carelessness nor responsibility for the repeated check; their causal relationship remains unknown.

New leads, colleagues, managers, learning teams and employee representatives are prospective affected groups. None have participated. This is a revised rehearsal Design brief, not approved requirements or demonstrated proficiency. The previous workforce journal remains an immutable parent, not a measured baseline or approved intervention.

Sequence 15 integrates the specialist drafts at sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Sequence 2 preserves parent material, including a hypothetical shared-workstation interruption. Sequence 18 introduces another hypothetical event: after a template-dependent proposal exists, an authorized fictional manager offers restored access on the condition that the colleague completes the note after their shift; coverage and protected time have been withdrawn. The fictional colleague refuses the additional work. Ownership remains unresolved. Neither hypothetical event is an observation or prediction.

Rival explanations include changed schedules, inaccessible materials, unclear ownership, inadequate coverage and conflicting expectations. Conversation difficulty may be secondary to those conditions. Training is not the automatic response.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: participants need room to question observations, retain tentative interpretations, reject feedback, correct wording, withhold agreement, choose written participation, pass or stop without justification. Leads must distinguish inquiry from decisions requiring another person’s authority. A colleague’s refusal does not become a capability judgment. Managers must inspect protected time, coverage, access, ownership and suitable space. Authority to restore access does not establish authority to resolve every workflow condition or another person’s agreement. Facilitators need covered time and accessible materials; they must not grade speech, speed, confidence, eye contact or script fidelity. No resources, support owners or participation protections are secured.

System requirements: use deterministic choices and explicitly authored fictional examples. Separate source facts, possible explanations, missing accounts, initial history, current proposals and pending corrections. Represent access, relevant authority, protected capacity and agreement independently. Protected capacity comprises protected time and coverage; if either is unavailable, the combined condition is unavailable, and an unresolved component remains unknown. Do not use a single available-support label as a feasibility certificate.

Use fictional inputs only. Exclude real employee records, identifiable recordings, profiling, employee ranking, consequential HR advice, automatic scores, telemetry, storage and network requests. Keep only volatile state in the candidate frame; refresh or closure loses work. No export, sharing controls, certificates, attendance logs or aid-use records are proposed. Do not evaluate optional text or infer consent, readiness, reactions or learning needs. Humans retain consequential workplace decisions and any separate disclosure decision.

Language needs, reading demands, devices, assistive technology, suitable space and workflow resources are unknown. Responsive layout, plain wording, untimed keyboard use and visible focus are intended qualities requiring inspection. Recording nothing cannot prevent informal observation or employment pressure.

## Experience and decisions

The main task produces one conversation proposal through brief choices rather than a long questionnaire. Begin with a linear situation board labelled Observed fictional facts, Possible explanations and Missing context. Show the absent note and repeated check as observations; explanations remain tentative, including when selected. Keep the unheard colleague account and uncertain causal relationship visible. Do not rely on color, dragging, hover or spatial position.

Offer exact opening previews: “I noticed Monday’s handoff note was absent. What was happening from your perspective?”; “Can we check how the handoff was meant to work on Monday?”; and “I need more context before deciding our next step.” Choose an opening and provisional next move without mandatory typing. Pass, Stop, Cover and Paper activity remain available without reasons. Explain session loss before entry; place detailed review metadata in Help.

Each opening changes an explicitly authored possible exchange and descriptive feedback. Include a colleague offering context, questioning an interpretation or asking to discuss it later. Label dialogue beside the preview as invented possibilities, not predicted reactions or evidence about people. Participants can reject examples and feedback, retain their proposal or retry an opening against another authored possibility. No branch receives praise, blame, scores or a preferred-answer marker.

Capture the Initial proposal before revealing the supplied context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague, and the expected owner was unclear. This adds information without proving a complete cause. Invite retaining or revising the interpretation and next move. Retaining wording must still display the new constraints.

For a next move involving template use or additional handoff work, reveal relevant dependency choices: access, authority to resolve the proposed condition, and protected time/coverage, each Available, Unavailable or Unknown within the fictional prospective situation. Show what authority is needed and what work remains unassigned. Offer checking expectations, requesting support or pausing. Unknown or unavailable conditions produce a conditional proposal, inquiry or pause; they never produce an unconditional commitment. Even available support leaves reciprocal agreement unresolved.

Introduce sequence 18’s changed-condition card after a template-dependent initial proposal exists. A pending correction may remain open when the participant activates the card so the recovery rule is inspectable. Display: “Access offered; protected capacity unavailable; colleague agreement withheld; ownership unresolved.” Display the authored response: “Making the template accessible does not give me time to complete it after my shift. I cannot agree to that extra work.” Label the event and response hypothetical. An offer to restore access is distinct from confirmed availability, and neither supplies time or agreement.

After that event, offer three concrete routes: request clarification of protected capacity and ownership; reconsider the next move; or pause. Authored synthesis must leave additional work unassigned and avoid promising after-shift completion. Retaining wording or rejecting feedback remains possible, with the conflict independently visible. Prospective support changes must not erase the recorded refusal or invent later agreement. They must also leave Monday’s inaccessible template, unclear owner and the withdrawal event intact as fictional history.

Show clearly labelled Initial proposal and Current proposal. Each contains observation, invitation, next move, relevant support, authority, protected capacity, unassigned work and unresolved questions or disagreement. State neutrally what changed or was retained. Put “Fictional practice proposal; no workplace agreement or capability judgment” beside the output. On narrow screens, versions may appear sequentially with explicit labels.

Feedback describes what wording states, whose account it invites and what remains unresolved. A carelessness interpretation remains an explanation rather than an observed cause. A process inquiry identifies the expectation being checked. Template use names access, ownership and capacity conditions. Pausing leaves a suitable opportunity and agreement unarranged. Feedback is contestable; revising is not itself success.

Use at most two optional main-path text fields: replacement wording and an unresolved question, both for fictional content only. A component selector identifies what the replacement changes. Review shows the exact replacement, affected component and dependency summary before Apply or Cancel. Cancel preserves the current proposal. Applied participant wording remains verbatim and labelled; the candidate cannot certify its feasibility. Independent conditions remain visible even if the text contradicts them.

A relevant context or support change, including sequence 18’s event, invalidates any pending correction review. Preserve the draft, mark the review stale and disable Apply until the participant explicitly reviews the exact replacement with the updated conditions. Renewed review enables a separate Apply decision; reviewing alone does not apply it. Cancel preserves current wording and the newly revealed conditions rather than reversing the event.

Cover immediately conceals all content surfaces, including scenario, history, current plans, text fields, pending reviews, dialogue, second-situation progress and open detail views. Concealed content must be unavailable through ordinary assistive-technology navigation. Move focus to a neutral screen. Resume is explicit, restores current corrections and the capacity conflict, and offers optional orientation without a recall task. Stale reviews remain stale. No automatic resumption, interruption logs or inactivity assessment.

Finish and clear for handoff is separate from Cover. Describe the scope and require confirmation; Cancel retains the session. Confirmation resets every candidate value and rendered surface, including both situations, initial/current plans, support and capacity choices, refusal state, drafts and pending previews, then shows a neutral start screen. Clearing must work from Cover without revealing content. Cover retains volatile work; clearing removes candidate session state. Neither prevents prior viewing or external capture.

Offer one optional second situation: “Two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check.” Begin with fewer suggestions and keep help immediately available without recording its use. Produce an ownership-focused opening and next move through choices. Keep its source data and state separate: do not inherit Monday’s access barrier or sequence 18’s refusal and capacity withdrawal. Call it supported practice, not a transfer test.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Inquiry and reciprocal agency. Origins: Workforce R1/R3, sequence 5; Systems SE2, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD1/HCD2, sequence 9; Learning scientist LS1–LS3, sequence 11; integrated in sequence 15. Interaction: labelled board, distinct opening previews, contestable feedback, context reveal, optional retry and before/after proposal. Human reason: participants need to examine ambiguity without conforming to a script or losing dissent. System reason: polished examples can imply diagnosis or predicted reactions. Check: complete without typing, exercise every opening, reject examples and feedback, retain a tentative interpretation and finish with unresolved disagreement or a pause. Inspect separate second-situation facts and available support. Relevance, language and feedback criteria remain unreviewed.

R2 — Separate feasibility conditions and agreement. Origins: Workforce R2, sequence 5; Systems SE1, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD3, sequence 9; Responsible AI RA1, sequence 13; sequence 15 R2; Scenario SC1, sequence 18. Interaction: distinguish access, authority, protected capacity and agreement; introduce capacity withdrawal after an initial proposal; offer clarification, reconsideration or pause. Human reason: usable tools and managerial authority do not supply time, coverage or consent. System reason: an available-support selection can otherwise conceal an unsupported commitment. Check: available access plus unavailable capacity and withheld agreement yields qualified wording, unassigned work and unresolved ownership, without after-shift promises. Prospective support changes preserve source history and refusal. Actual resources, authority and workload arrangements remain unknown.

R3 — Correction, recovery and equivalent alternatives. Origins: hypothetical interruption preserved at sequence 2; Workforce R4/R5, sequence 5; Systems SE3/SE4, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD4/HCD5, sequence 9; Learning scientist LS4, sequence 11; Responsible AI RA2–RA4, sequence 13; sequence 15 R3; Scenario SC1, sequence 18. Interaction: exact review/Apply/Cancel, stale-review handling, complete Cover, explicit Resume, confirmed handoff clearing and direct paper access. Human reason: interruption and dissent require control without memory tests or loss of refusal. System reason: stale previews and partial resets can expose or restore rejected content. Check: introduce withdrawal during review, require renewed inspection, cancel without reversing the event, cover/resume the corrected state and confirm complete clearing from Cover. Inspect keyboard focus, concealment, narrow layout and prohibited technical behavior. Run the full paper task. No checks have occurred.

Choices reduce entry burden but constrain expression; optional correction and unresolved questions preserve another route. Examples support participation but can invite imitation; rejecting them and requesting help remain legitimate. Dependency details add work, so reveal them when the next move requires them. Before/after comparison makes revision inspectable without rewarding change.

Retain dissent that organizational repair or no practice is preferable. An accountable review of rota, coverage, protected time, ownership and accessible materials is a non-learning option. The candidate cannot authorize repairs. Deterministic browser practice and facilitated paper practice are non-AI options; neither secures participation protections.

Complete paper materials: a situation card containing the three initial story statements; a board labelled Observed facts, Possible explanations and Missing context; the three exact opening cards above; blank replacement, Pass and Stop cards. A reveal card states the changed rota, inaccessible template and unclear owner, labelled invented context rather than a complete cause. Authored response cards say “Here is additional context”, “I question that interpretation” and “I would prefer to discuss this later”, labelled possibilities rather than predictions.

Provide Initial proposal and Current proposal sheets with spaces for observation, invitation, next move, access, authority, protected time/coverage, agreement, unassigned work and unresolved questions. Supply Available, Unavailable and Unknown cards for support conditions; agreement remains separately unresolved or withheld. Add sequence 18’s complete changed-condition card and exact refusal above. Add a feedback card asking: “Which wording is observation or explanation?”, “Whose account or agreement is missing?” and “What support makes the move feasible?” Include a blank cover sheet and the exact second-situation card, with opening suggestions available on request.

Facilitation: arrange voluntary participation, protected time, accessible materials, suitable space and participant-controlled disposal first. Present the situation, invite an opening or Pass, and record the initial proposal. Release the reveal; for a template-dependent proposal, release the changed-condition card after the initial plan exists. Preserve refusal and leave additional work unassigned. Invite retention, one-component revision or stopping; describe implications without grading. Show the exact replacement and conditions before accepting it; cancellation preserves the current sheet. If conditions change during review, review again before acceptance. Offer an optional response-card retry or the separate second situation. Written selection is sufficient; speech and role-play are optional. Cover for interruption and resume only by participant choice. Do not solicit personal accounts, collect or photograph sheets, grade aid use, record attendance for assessment or require sharing. Dispose under the participant-controlled arrangement. These conditions are not secured.

## Acceptance checks

Plan fictional task walkthroughs for all openings, retained interpretations, rejected feedback, inaccessible templates, disputed ownership and postponed discussion. Complete with blank optional fields. Inspect faithful source distinctions, useful output and absence of scores or implied agreement.

Plan a capacity and recovery walkthrough: preserve an initial template proposal, open correction review, reveal sequence 18’s event, inspect stale-review handling and qualified output, renew review, cancel, cover and resume. Inspect preserved refusal and current wording; cancel clearing once, then confirm from Cover and inspect both situations and all state reset. Separately inspect keyboard behavior, concealed accessibility content, responsive layout, code and runtime for storage, tracking and network requests. These are planned checks, not observed behavior.

Pending practitioner, affected-person and representative review must examine comprehension, credible refusal, reciprocal dignity, belonging, language, device access, sustainable workload, screen visibility and paper handling. Technical verification would establish only inspected behavior, not free participation, learning, retention, transfer or flourishing.

## Evidence and unknowns

Sequence 15 supplies the previous integrated Design and its specialist origins; sequence 18 supplies the hypothetical capacity conflict. Neither is empirical evidence. Sequence 2’s preservation event does not approve the preserved material. No participant observations, consensus, human approval, technical results, field pilot or empirical success exists. Field evidence remains pending.

The concrete change from sequence 15 is independent protected-capacity representation, an actionable withdrawal/refusal state, renewed correction review and complete recovery coverage of those values. Preserve its inquiry, access, authority, disagreement and paper requirements. Design is the earliest supplied interaction artifact invalidated by this event; the material does not establish an omission in Map.

Unknowns include task relevance, local shift arrangements, authority to secure protected time, credible refusal, acceptable feedback and added burden. Apparent improvement could reflect copied examples, familiarity, facilitator cues, selective participation or repaired workflow. Difficulty could reflect language, reading demands, workload or dissent rather than a capability deficit. Immediate supported performance, delayed retention and adaptation in changed workplace conditions require different evidence; none is established here.

## Next decision

Replace sequence 15’s Design brief with this targeted revision, then implement a focused deterministic rehearsal Build. Exercise the planned fictional technical cases and prepare practitioner and affected-person interaction review. Keep intended quality, subsequently observed technical behavior and untested learning and flourishing separate. This is one Design revision, with no request to reopen Map. What was happening from your perspective?”; “Can we check how the handoff was meant to work on Monday?”; and “I need more context before deciding our next step.” Choose an opening and provisional next move without mandatory typing. Pass, Stop, Cover and Paper activity remain available without reasons. Explain session loss before entry; place detailed review metadata in Help.

Each opening changes an explicitly authored possible exchange and descriptive feedback. Include a colleague offering context, questioning an interpretation or asking to discuss it later. Label dialogue beside the preview as invented possibilities, not predicted reactions or evidence about people. Participants can reject examples and feedback, retain their proposal or retry an opening against another authored possibility. No branch receives praise, blame, scores or a preferred-answer marker.

Capture the Initial proposal before revealing the supplied context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague, and the expected owner was unclear. This adds information without proving a complete cause. Invite retaining or revising the interpretation and next move. Retaining wording must still display the new constraints.

For a next move involving template use or additional handoff work, reveal relevant dependency choices: access, authority to resolve the proposed condition, and protected time/coverage, each Available, Unavailable or Unknown within the fictional prospective situation. Show what authority is needed and what work remains unassigned. Offer checking expectations, requesting support or pausing. Unknown or unavailable conditions produce a conditional proposal, inquiry or pause; they never produce an unconditional commitment. Even available support leaves reciprocal agreement unresolved.

Introduce sequence 18’s changed-condition card after a template-dependent initial proposal exists. A pending correction may remain open when the participant activates the card so the recovery rule is inspectable. Display: “Access offered; protected capacity unavailable; colleague agreement withheld; ownership unresolved.” Display the authored response: “Making the template accessible does not give me time to complete it after my shift. I cannot agree to that extra work.” Label the event and response hypothetical. An offer to restore access is distinct from confirmed availability, and neither supplies time or agreement.

After that event, offer three concrete routes: request clarification of protected capacity and ownership; reconsider the next move; or pause. Authored synthesis must leave additional work unassigned and avoid promising after-shift completion. Retaining wording or rejecting feedback remains possible, with the conflict independently visible. Prospective support changes must not erase the recorded refusal or invent later agreement. They must also leave Monday’s inaccessible template, unclear owner and the withdrawal event intact as fictional history.

Show clearly labelled Initial proposal and Current proposal. Each contains observation, invitation, next move, relevant support, authority, protected capacity, unassigned work and unresolved questions or disagreement. State neutrally what changed or was retained. Put “Fictional practice proposal; no workplace agreement or capability judgment” beside the output. On narrow screens, versions may appear sequentially with explicit labels.

Feedback describes what wording states, whose account it invites and what remains unresolved. A carelessness interpretation remains an explanation rather than an observed cause. A process inquiry identifies the expectation being checked. Template use names access, ownership and capacity conditions. Pausing leaves a suitable opportunity and agreement unarranged. Feedback is contestable; revising is not itself success.

Use at most two optional main-path text fields: replacement wording and an unresolved question, both for fictional content only. A component selector identifies what the replacement changes. Review shows the exact replacement, affected component and dependency summary before Apply or Cancel. Cancel preserves the current proposal. Applied participant wording remains verbatim and labelled; the candidate cannot certify its feasibility. Independent conditions remain visible even if the text contradicts them.

A relevant context or support change, including sequence 18’s event, invalidates any pending correction review. Preserve the draft, mark the review stale and disable Apply until the participant explicitly reviews the exact replacement with the updated conditions. Renewed review enables a separate Apply decision; reviewing alone does not apply it. Cancel preserves current wording and the newly revealed conditions rather than reversing the event.

Cover immediately conceals all content surfaces, including scenario, history, current plans, text fields, pending reviews, dialogue, second-situation progress and open detail views. Concealed content must be unavailable through ordinary assistive-technology navigation. Move focus to a neutral screen. Resume is explicit, restores current corrections and the capacity conflict, and offers optional orientation without a recall task. Stale reviews remain stale. No automatic resumption, interruption logs or inactivity assessment.

Finish and clear for handoff is separate from Cover. Describe the scope and require confirmation; Cancel retains the session. Confirmation resets every candidate value and rendered surface, including both situations, initial/current plans, support and capacity choices, refusal state, drafts and pending previews, then shows a neutral start screen. Clearing must work from Cover without revealing content. Cover retains volatile work; clearing removes candidate session state. Neither prevents prior viewing or external capture.

Offer one optional second situation: “Two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check.” Begin with fewer suggestions and keep help immediately available without recording its use. Produce an ownership-focused opening and next move through choices. Keep its source data and state separate: do not inherit Monday’s access barrier or sequence 18’s refusal and capacity withdrawal.
