## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Inquiry and reciprocal agency. Origins: Workforce R1/R3, sequence 5; Systems SE2, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD1/HCD2, sequence 9; Learning scientist LS1–LS3, sequence 11; integrated in sequence 15. Interaction: labelled board, distinct opening previews, contestable feedback, context reveal, optional retry and before/after proposal. Human reason: participants need to examine ambiguity without conforming to a script or losing dissent. System reason: polished examples can imply diagnosis or predicted reactions. Check: complete without typing, exercise every opening, reject examples and feedback, retain a tentative interpretation and finish with unresolved disagreement or a pause. Inspect separate second-situation facts and available support. Relevance, language and feedback criteria remain unreviewed.

R2 — Separate feasibility conditions and agreement. Origins: Workforce R2, sequence 5; Systems SE1, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD3, sequence 9; Responsible AI RA1, sequence 13; sequence 15 R2; Scenario SC1, sequence 18. Interaction: distinguish access, authority, protected capacity and agreement; introduce capacity withdrawal after an initial proposal; offer clarification, reconsideration or pause. Human reason: usable tools and managerial authority do not supply time, coverage or consent. System reason: an available-support selection can otherwise conceal an unsupported commitment. Check: available access plus unavailable capacity and withheld agreement yields qualified wording, unassigned work and unresolved ownership, without after-shift promises. Prospective support changes preserve source history and refusal. Actual resources, authority and workload arrangements remain unknown.

R3 — Correction, recovery and equivalent alternatives. Origins: hypothetical interruption preserved at sequence 2; Workforce R4/R5, sequence 5; Systems SE3/SE4, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD4/HCD5, sequence 9; Learning scientist LS4, sequence 11; Responsible AI RA2–RA4, sequence 13; sequence 15 R3; Scenario SC1, sequence 18. Interaction: exact review/Apply/Cancel, stale-review handling, complete Cover, explicit Resume, confirmed handoff clearing and direct paper access. Human reason: interruption and dissent require control without memory tests or loss of refusal. System reason: stale previews and partial resets can expose or restore rejected content. Check: introduce withdrawal during review, require renewed inspection, cancel without reversing the event, cover/resume the corrected state and confirm complete clearing from Cover. Inspect keyboard focus, concealment, narrow layout and prohibited technical behavior. Run the full paper task. No checks have occurred.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Choices reduce entry burden but constrain expression; optional correction and unresolved questions preserve another route. Examples support participation but can invite imitation; rejecting them and requesting help remain legitimate. Dependency details add work, so reveal them when the next move requires them. Before/after comparison makes revision inspectable without rewarding change.

Retain dissent that organizational repair or no practice is preferable. An accountable review of rota, coverage, protected time, ownership and accessible materials is a non-learning option. The candidate cannot authorize repairs. Deterministic browser practice and facilitated paper practice are non-AI options; neither secures participation protections.

Complete paper materials: a situation card containing the three initial story statements; a board labelled Observed facts, Possible explanations and Missing context; the three exact opening cards above; blank replacement, Pass and Stop cards. A reveal card states the changed rota, inaccessible template and unclear owner, labelled invented context rather than a complete cause. Authored response cards say “Here is additional context”, “I question that interpretation” and “I would prefer to discuss this later”, labelled possibilities rather than predictions.

Provide Initial proposal and Current proposal sheets with spaces for observation, invitation, next move, access, authority, protected time/coverage, agreement, unassigned work and unresolved questions. Supply Available, Unavailable and Unknown cards for support conditions; agreement remains separately unresolved or withheld. Add sequence 18’s complete changed-condition card and exact refusal above. Add a feedback card asking: “Which wording is observation or explanation?”, “Whose account or agreement is missing?” and “What support makes the move feasible?” Include a blank cover sheet and the exact second-situation card, with opening suggestions available on request.

Facilitation: arrange voluntary participation, protected time, accessible materials, suitable space and participant-controlled disposal first. Present the situation, invite an opening or Pass, and record the initial proposal. Release the reveal; for a template-dependent proposal, release the changed-condition card after the initial plan exists. Preserve refusal and leave additional work unassigned. Invite retention, one-component revision or stopping; describe implications without grading. Show the exact replacement and conditions before accepting it; cancellation preserves the current sheet. If conditions change during review, review again before acceptance. Offer an optional response-card retry or the separate second situation. Written selection is sufficient; speech and role-play are optional. Cover for interruption and resume only by participant choice. Do not solicit personal accounts, collect or photograph sheets, grade aid use, record attendance for assessment or require sharing. Dispose under the participant-controlled arrangement. These conditions are not secured.

## Acceptance checks

Plan fictional task walkthroughs for all openings, retained interpretations, rejected feedback, inaccessible templates, disputed ownership and postponed discussion. Complete with blank optional fields. Inspect faithful source distinctions, useful output and absence of scores or implied agreement.

Plan a capacity and recovery walkthrough: preserve an initial template proposal, open correction review, reveal sequence 18’s event, inspect stale-review handling and qualified output, renew review, cancel, cover and resume. Inspect preserved refusal and current wording; cancel clearing once, then confirm from Cover and inspect both situations and all state reset. Separately inspect keyboard behavior, concealed accessibility content, responsive layout, code and runtime for storage, tracking and network requests. These are planned checks, not observed behavior.

Pending practitioner, affected-person and representative review must examine comprehension, credible refusal, reciprocal dignity, belonging, language, device access, sustainable workload, screen visibility and paper handling. Technical verification would establish only inspected behavior, not free participation, learning, retention, transfer or flourishing.

## Evidence and unknowns

Sequence 15 supplies the previous integrated Design and its specialist origins; sequence 18 supplies the hypothetical capacity conflict. Neither is empirical evidence. Sequence 2’s preservation event does not approve the preserved material. No participant observations, consensus, human approval, technical results, field pilot or empirical success exists. Field evidence remains pending.

The concrete change from sequence 15 is independent protected-capacity representation, an actionable withdrawal/refusal state, renewed correction review and complete recovery coverage of those values. Preserve its inquiry, access, authority, disagreement and paper requirements. Design is the earliest supplied interaction artifact invalidated by this event; the material does not establish an omission in Map.

Unknowns include task relevance, local shift arrangements, authority to secure protected time, credible refusal, acceptable feedback and added burden. Apparent improvement could reflect copied examples, familiarity, facilitator cues, selective participation or repaired workflow. Difficulty could reflect language, reading demands, workload or dissent rather than a capability deficit. Immediate supported performance, delayed retention and adaptation in changed workplace conditions require different evidence; none is established here.

## Next decision

Replace sequence 15’s Design brief with this targeted revision, then implement a focused deterministic rehearsal Build. Exercise the planned fictional technical cases and prepare practitioner and affected-person interaction review. Keep intended quality, subsequently observed technical behavior and untested learning and flourishing separate. This is one Design revision, with no request to reopen Map. This Evaluate contribution reviews supplied evidence, not an independently inspected executable. Sequence 2 preserves the parent rehearsal as background, not a baseline. Sequence 18 is a hypothetical objection; sequence 20 revises Design around independent capacity and withheld agreement. Sequence 32 reports implementation checks. Event 38 supplies actual host technical observations tied to artifact 35 and its recorded hash. The iteration requested Design and Build before this technical review; Instrument/Deploy and a human pilot were not rerun.

Source and offline evidence: event 38 reports an independent syntax check, a passing focused Node helper and broader integration/package checks. These support the checked source and helper assertions. Stub/pure-state execution does not establish browser behavior, scientific validity or human capability. The Build brief's source inspection reports no apparent prohibited operations; the packet does not establish a comprehensive runtime network, storage or privacy audit.

Exercised browser evidence: event 38 reports facts/openings, reveal and before/after history, stale review after withdrawal, renewed review and exact Apply, independent prospective support choices, Cover/Resume, separate second-situation state, rendered paper materials and confirmed clearing. Keyboard Enter focused main#content through the corrected skip button. No horizontal overflow was observed at 1280 pixels and no console errors were recorded. These are actual scoped observations, not hypothetical scenarios. Coverage does not establish every path, narrow-screen usability, complete concealment from assistive navigation or comprehensive accessibility. The helper's reset assertions supplement the visible clearing observation; they do not expand browser coverage.

Acceptance requirement M1: at the board, opening selection and reveal, preserve the distinction between observation, tentative explanation and missing account so a learner can inquire without inferred fault. Accept the exercised technical paths on event 38's labels, authored previews and preserved initial record. Still check completion with blank optional fields, rejected feedback, retained interpretations, Pass and Stop. Do not require revision or script fidelity as success. Human comprehension and usefulness remain unknown.

Acceptance requirement M2: when conditions change during exact correction review, preserve the draft, disable stale Apply, require renewed review and a separate Apply decision, and let Cancel preserve both committed wording and new conditions. This protects correction and dissent. Event 38 meets this scoped technical check. Its prospective Available selections also left agreement withheld and extra work unassigned, addressing sequence 18's challenge without erasing history. Human recognition of these distinctions remains untested.

Acceptance requirement M3: at interruption and handoff, let people Cover, explicitly Resume, cancel clearing or confirm complete clearing, including the second situation and pending drafts. Event 38 supports exercised recovery and visible clearing, with offline reset support. Require a later full keyboard, focus, assistive-navigation, magnification and narrow-layout inspection before claiming accessible recovery. Paper materials were rendered; inspect print layout and conduct a complete fictional paper walkthrough before claiming equivalent practical access. Retain written selection, passing, stopping and participant-controlled disposal.

Future human evidence must be separately authorized and reviewed; this packet grants none. Review task relevance, comprehension, credible refusal and burden with prospective new leads and affected-person perspectives, including varied language, reading, device and accessibility needs. Compare browser and complete paper participation without grading speech, confidence or aid use. Keep all candidate inputs fictional and add no candidate telemetry, storage, recordings or employee assessment.

For any later learning claim, define observable task evidence in advance: distinguish facts from explanations, invite a missing account, and identify unresolved agreement and necessary workflow support. Preserve defensible retention, pause and dissent. Use unfamiliar fictional cases and comparisons that address copied examples, practice familiarity and facilitator cues. Immediate supported performance, delayed retention and adaptation across changed conditions require distinct evidence. The second situation alone supplies none of those conclusions; workplace transfer and flourishing remain absent.

Decision: accept only the inspected technical behavior for continued review. No supplied finding requires another Build revision, but untested requirements remain open. Retain organizational repair, complete paper facilitation and no practice as legitimate alternatives. Human approval, field readiness, learning, transfer and flourishing are not established.

Conversation Lab proposes voluntary practice for first-time team leads using an invented missed-handoff story: a handoff note was absent on Monday, the next shift repeated a check, and the lead has not heard the colleague’s account. The task is to distinguish observation from explanation, choose an opening, reconsider changed information and prepare a feasible conversation proposal. New leads, colleagues, managers, learning teams and employee representatives are prospective affected groups. None have participated. This is a revised rehearsal Design brief, not approved requirements or demonstrated proficiency. The previous workforce journal remains an immutable parent, not a measured baseline or approved intervention.

Sequence 15 integrates the specialist drafts at sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Sequence 2 preserves parent material, including a hypothetical shared-workstation interruption. Sequence 18 introduces another hypothetical event: after a template-dependent proposal exists, an authorized fictional manager offers restored access on the condition that the colleague completes the note after their shift; coverage and protected time have been withdrawn. The fictional colleague refuses the additional work. Ownership remains unresolved. Neither hypothetical event is an observation or prediction.

Rival explanations include changed schedules, inaccessible materials, unclear ownership, inadequate coverage and conflicting expectations. Conversation difficulty may be secondary to those conditions. Training is not the automatic response.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: participants need room to question observations, retain tentative interpretations, reject feedback, correct wording, withhold agreement, choose written participation, pass or stop without justification. Leads must distinguish inquiry from decisions requiring another person’s authority. A colleague’s refusal does not become a capability judgment. Managers must inspect protected time, coverage, access, ownership and suitable space. Authority to restore access does not establish authority to resolve every workflow condition or another person’s agreement. Facilitators need covered time and accessible materials; they must not grade speech, speed, confidence, eye contact or script fidelity. No resources, support owners or participation protections are secured.

System requirements: use deterministic choices and explicitly authored fictional examples. Separate source facts, possible explanations, missing accounts, initial history, current proposals and pending corrections. Represent access, relevant authority, protected capacity and agreement independently. Protected capacity comprises protected time and coverage; if either is unavailable, the combined condition is unavailable, and an unresolved component remains unknown. Do not use a single available-support label as a feasibility certificate.

Use fictional inputs only. Exclude real employee records, identifiable recordings, profiling, employee ranking, consequential HR advice, automatic scores, telemetry, storage and network requests. Keep only volatile state in the candidate frame; refresh or closure loses work. No export, sharing controls, certificates, attendance logs or aid-use records are proposed. Do not evaluate optional text or infer consent, readiness, reactions or learning needs. Humans retain consequential workplace decisions and any separate disclosure decision.

Language needs, reading demands, devices, assistive technology, suitable space and workflow resources are unknown. Responsive layout, plain wording, untimed keyboard use and visible focus are intended qualities requiring inspection. Recording nothing cannot prevent informal observation or employment pressure.

## Experience and decisions

The main task produces one conversation proposal through brief choices rather than a long questionnaire. Begin with a linear situation board labelled Observed fictional facts, Possible explanations and Missing context. Show the absent note and repeated check as observations; explanations remain tentative, including when selected. Keep the unheard colleague account and uncertain causal relationship visible. Do not rely on color, dragging, hover or spatial position.

Offer exact opening previews: “I noticed Monday’s handoff note was absent. What was happening from your perspective?”; “Can we check how the handoff was meant to work on Monday?”; and “I need more context before deciding our next step.” Choose an opening and provisional next move without mandatory typing. Pass, Stop, Cover and Paper activity remain available without reasons. Explain session loss before entry; place detailed review metadata in Help.

Each opening changes an explicitly authored possible exchange and descriptive feedback. Include a colleague offering context, questioning an interpretation or asking to discuss it later. Label dialogue beside the preview as invented possibilities, not predicted reactions or evidence about people. Participants can reject examples and feedback, retain their proposal or retry an opening against another authored possibility. No branch receives praise, blame, scores or a preferred-answer marker.

Capture the Initial proposal before revealing the supplied context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague, and the expected owner was unclear. This adds information without proving a complete cause. Invite retaining or revising the interpretation and next move. Retaining wording must still display the new constraints.

For a next move involving template use or additional handoff work, reveal relevant dependency choices: access, authority to resolve the proposed condition, and protected time/coverage, each Available, Unavailable or Unknown within the fictional prospective situation. Show what authority is needed and what work remains unassigned. Offer checking expectations, requesting support or pausing. Unknown or unavailable conditions produce a conditional proposal, inquiry or pause; they never produce an unconditional commitment. Even available support leaves reciprocal agreement unresolved.

Introduce sequence 18’s changed-condition card after a template-dependent initial proposal exists. A pending correction may remain open when the participant activates the card so the recovery rule is inspectable. Display: “Access offered; protected capacity unavailable; colleague agreement withheld; ownership unresolved.” Display the authored response: “Making the template accessible does not give me time to complete it after my shift. I cannot agree to that extra work.” Label the event and response hypothetical. An offer to restore access is distinct from confirmed availability, and neither supplies time or agreement.

After that event, offer three concrete routes: request clarification of protected capacity and ownership; reconsider the next move; or pause. Authored synthesis must leave additional work unassigned and avoid promising after-shift completion. Retaining wording or rejecting feedback remains possible, with the conflict independently visible. Prospective support changes must not erase the recorded refusal or invent later agreement. They must also leave Monday’s inaccessible template, unclear owner and the withdrawal event intact as fictional history.

Show clearly labelled Initial proposal and Current proposal. Each contains observation, invitation, next move, relevant support, authority, protected capacity, unassigned work and unresolved questions or disagreement. State neutrally what changed or was retained. Put “Fictional practice proposal; no workplace agreement or capability judgment” beside the output. On narrow screens, versions may appear sequentially with explicit labels.

Feedback describes what wording states, whose account it invites and what remains unresolved. A carelessness interpretation remains an explanation rather than an observed cause. A process inquiry identifies the expectation being checked. Template use names access, ownership and capacity conditions. Pausing leaves a suitable opportunity and agreement unarranged. Feedback is contestable; revising is not itself success.

Use at most two optional main-path text fields: replacement wording and an unresolved question, both for fictional content only. A component selector identifies what the replacement changes. Review shows the exact replacement, affected component and dependency summary before Apply or Cancel. Cancel preserves the current proposal. Applied participant wording remains verbatim and labelled; the candidate cannot certify its feasibility. Independent conditions remain visible even if the text contradicts them.

A relevant context or support change, including sequence 18’s event, invalidates any pending correction review. Preserve the draft, mark the review stale and disable Apply until the participant explicitly reviews the exact replacement with the updated conditions. Renewed review enables a separate Apply decision; reviewing alone does not apply it. Cancel preserves current wording and the newly revealed conditions rather than reversing the event.

Cover immediately conceals all content surfaces, including scenario, history, current plans, text fields, pending reviews, dialogue, second-situation progress and open detail views. Concealed content must be unavailable through ordinary assistive-technology navigation. Move focus to a neutral screen. Resume is explicit, restores current corrections and the capacity conflict, and offers optional orientation without a recall task. Stale reviews remain stale. No automatic resumption, interruption logs or inactivity assessment.

Finish and clear for handoff is separate from Cover. Describe the scope and require confirmation; Cancel retains the session. Confirmation resets every candidate value and rendered surface, including both situations, initial/current plans, support and capacity choices, refusal state, drafts and pending previews, then shows a neutral start screen. Clearing must work from Cover without revealing content. Cover retains volatile work; clearing removes candidate session state. Neither prevents prior viewing or external capture.

Offer one optional second situation: “Two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check.” Begin with fewer suggestions and keep help immediately available without recording its use. Produce an ownership-focused opening and next move through choices. Keep its source data and state separate: do not inherit Monday’s access barrier or sequence 18’s refusal and capacity withdrawal. Call it supported practice, not a transfer test.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Inquiry and reciprocal agency. Origins: Workforce R1/R3, sequence 5; Systems SE2, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD1/HCD2, sequence 9; Learning scientist LS1–LS3, sequence 11; integrated in sequence 15. Interaction: labelled board, distinct opening previews, contestable feedback, context reveal, optional retry and before/after proposal. Human reason: participants need to examine ambiguity without conforming to a script or losing dissent. System reason: polished examples can imply diagnosis or predicted reactions. Check: complete without typing, exercise every opening, reject examples and feedback, retain a tentative interpretation and finish with unresolved disagreement or a pause. Inspect separate second-situation facts and available support. Relevance, language and feedback criteria remain unreviewed.

R2 — Separate feasibility conditions and agreement. Origins: Workforce R2, sequence 5; Systems SE1, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD3, sequence 9; Responsible AI RA1, sequence 13; sequence 15 R2; Scenario SC1, sequence 18. Interaction: distinguish access, authority, protected capacity and agreement; introduce capacity withdrawal after an initial proposal; offer clarification, reconsideration or pause. Human reason: usable tools and managerial authority do not supply time, coverage or consent. System reason: an available-support selection can otherwise conceal an unsupported commitment. Check: available access plus unavailable capacity and withheld agreement yields qualified wording, unassigned work and unresolved ownership, without after-shift promises. Prospective support changes preserve source history and refusal. Actual resources, authority and workload arrangements remain unknown.

R3 — Correction, recovery and equivalent alternatives. Origins: hypothetical interruption preserved at sequence 2; Workforce R4/R5, sequence 5; Systems SE3/SE4, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD4/HCD5, sequence 9; Learning scientist LS4, sequence 11; Responsible AI RA2–RA4, sequence 13; sequence 15 R3; Scenario SC1, sequence 18. Interaction: exact review/Apply/Cancel, stale-review handling, complete Cover, explicit Resume, confirmed handoff clearing and direct paper access. Human reason: interruption and dissent require control without memory tests or loss of refusal. System reason: stale previews and partial resets can expose or restore rejected content. Check: introduce withdrawal during review, require renewed inspection, cancel without reversing the event, cover/resume the corrected state and confirm complete clearing from Cover. Inspect keyboard focus, concealment, narrow layout and prohibited technical behavior. Run the full paper task. No checks have occurred.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Choices reduce entry burden but constrain expression; optional correction and unresolved questions preserve another route. Examples support participation but can invite imitation; rejecting them and requesting help remain legitimate. Dependency details add work, so reveal them when the next move requires them. Before/after comparison makes revision inspectable without rewarding change.

Retain dissent that organizational repair or no practice is preferable. An accountable review of rota, coverage, protected time, ownership and accessible materials is a non-learning option. The candidate cannot authorize repairs. Deterministic browser practice and facilitated paper practice are non-AI options; neither secures participation protections.

Complete paper materials: a situation card containing the three initial story statements; a board labelled Observed facts, Possible explanations and Missing context; the three exact opening cards above; blank replacement, Pass and Stop cards. A reveal card states the changed rota, inaccessible template and unclear owner, labelled invented context rather than a complete cause. Authored response cards say “Here is additional context”, “I question that interpretation” and “I would prefer to discuss this later”, labelled possibilities rather than predictions.

Provide Initial proposal and Current proposal sheets with spaces for observation, invitation, next move, access, authority, protected time/coverage, agreement, unassigned work and unresolved questions. Supply Available, Unavailable and Unknown cards for support conditions; agreement remains separately unresolved or withheld. Add sequence 18’s complete changed-condition card and exact refusal above. Add a feedback card asking: “Which wording is observation or explanation?”, “Whose account or agreement is missing?” and “What support makes the move feasible?” Include a blank cover sheet and the exact second-situation card, with opening suggestions available on request.

Facilitation: arrange voluntary participation, protected time, accessible materials, suitable space and participant-controlled disposal first. Present the situation, invite an opening or Pass, and record the initial proposal. Release the reveal; for a template-dependent proposal, release the changed-condition card after the initial plan exists. Preserve refusal and leave additional work unassigned. Invite retention, one-component revision or stopping; describe implications without grading. Show the exact replacement and conditions before accepting it; cancellation preserves the current sheet. If conditions change during review, review again before acceptance. Offer an optional response-card retry or the separate second situation. Written selection is sufficient; speech and role-play are optional. Cover for interruption and resume only by participant choice. Do not solicit personal accounts, collect or photograph sheets, grade aid use, record attendance for assessment or require sharing. Dispose under the participant-controlled arrangement. These conditions are not secured.

## Acceptance checks

Plan fictional task walkthroughs for all openings, retained interpretations, rejected feedback, inaccessible templates, disputed ownership and postponed discussion. Complete with blank optional fields. Inspect faithful source distinctions, useful output and absence of scores or implied agreement.

Plan a capacity and recovery walkthrough: preserve an initial template proposal, open correction review, reveal sequence 18’s event, inspect stale-review handling and qualified output, renew review, cancel, cover and resume. Inspect preserved refusal and current wording; cancel clearing once, then confirm from Cover and inspect both situations and all state reset. Separately inspect keyboard behavior, concealed accessibility content, responsive layout, code and runtime for storage, tracking and network requests. These are planned checks, not observed behavior.

Pending practitioner, affected-person and representative review must examine comprehension, credible refusal, reciprocal dignity, belonging, language, device access, sustainable workload, screen visibility and paper handling. Technical verification would establish only inspected behavior, not free participation, learning, retention, transfer or flourishing.

## Evidence and unknowns

Sequence 15 supplies the previous integrated Design and its specialist origins; sequence 18 supplies the hypothetical capacity conflict. Neither is empirical evidence. Sequence 2’s preservation event does not approve the preserved material. No participant observations, consensus, human approval, technical results, field pilot or empirical success exists. Field evidence remains pending.

The concrete change from sequence 15 is independent protected-capacity representation, an actionable withdrawal/refusal state, renewed correction review and complete recovery coverage of those values. Preserve its inquiry, access, authority, disagreement and paper requirements. Design is the earliest supplied interaction artifact invalidated by this event; the material does not establish an omission in Map.

Unknowns include task relevance, local shift arrangements, authority to secure protected time, credible refusal, acceptable feedback and added burden. Apparent improvement could reflect copied examples, familiarity, facilitator cues, selective participation or repaired workflow. Difficulty could reflect language, reading demands, workload or dissent rather than a capability deficit. Immediate supported performance, delayed retention and adaptation in changed workplace conditions require different evidence; none is established here.

## Next decision

Replace sequence 15’s Design brief with this targeted revision, then implement a focused deterministic rehearsal Build. Exercise the planned fictional technical cases and prepare practitioner and affected-person interaction review. Keep intended quality, subsequently observed technical behavior and untested learning and flourishing separate. This is one Design revision, with no request to reopen Map. Decision and scope
Accept only the technical behavior exercised in event 38 for continued candidate review. No supplied observation demonstrates a blocking defect requiring another Design or Build revision. Open checks remain open; this decision establishes neither human approval nor field readiness and authorizes no pilot. Design and Build were the requested iteration stages before this Evaluate review. The preserved parent eight-stage rehearsal is background, not a baseline or newly executed sequence. Instrument/Deploy and human testing were not rerun.

Evidence register
Event 38 is actual host technical evidence tied to artifact 35 and its recorded content hash. It is distinct from the hypothetical withdrawal/refusal event used in the fictional activity. This contribution synthesizes the supplied receipt and earlier review at sequence 41; it does not independently inspect executable source.

Source/offline evidence: event 38 reports an independent inline-source syntax check, a passing focused Node helper and broader lifecycle, packaging and site checks. These support their checked assertions. Stub/pure-state checks do not establish browser behavior, scientific validity or human capability. The Build brief reports no apparent prohibited source operations; a comprehensive runtime network, storage and privacy audit is not established.

Browser evidence: event 38 exercised facts and three openings, context reveal and before/after history, stale correction after changed conditions, renewed review and exact Apply, prospective support changes, Cover/Resume, separate second-situation behavior, rendered paper materials and confirmed clearing. Cancel preserved committed wording and new conditions. Available prospective support did not erase withheld agreement or assign extra work. Enter on the corrected skip button focused main#content. No horizontal overflow was observed at 1280 pixels and no console errors were recorded. Visible clearing and offline reset assertions are separate evidence. These observations do not establish every path, complete assistive-navigation concealment or comprehensive accessibility.

Requirement disposition
R1, inquiry and reciprocal agency: accept the exercised technical distinctions between fictional observations, tentative explanations, missing context and authored possibilities, including preserved initial history. Completion with blank optional fields, rejected feedback, retained interpretations, Pass and Stop still needs inspection. Human comprehension, useful inquiry and credible refusal remain unknown; revision and script fidelity must not count as success.

R2, independent feasibility and agreement: accept the exercised stale-review and prospective-support cases. Exact drafts survived changed conditions; Apply required renewed review; cancellation preserved the event. Withheld agreement and unassigned work remained visible despite Available support selections. This addresses the fictional requirement challenge without proving that people understand those distinctions or that real capacity and authority exist.

R3, correction, recovery and alternatives: accept exercised Cover/Resume and confirmed clearing, bounded by the reported environment and helper assertions. Keep full keyboard/focus, assistive-navigation concealment, magnification and narrow-layout checks open. Paper materials were rendered, including cards, proposal sheets, correction and facilitator sequence. Print layout, physical handling and a complete fictional facilitated walkthrough remain untested.

Refinement record
Already implemented before this review, according to the supplied Build record and event 38: independent capacity/refusal representation, stale-review recovery with exact draft preservation, separate practice state, confirmed clearing and the corrected skip-to-content button. Event 38 supports the exercised portions of those changes; it does not certify all implementation paths. No new code is supplied or built in this turn.

Future proposals remain unbuilt: complete the outstanding interface, runtime privacy and paper checks; retain the current product unless a concrete failure identifies a necessary change. Any later Refine contribution must name the observed requirement failure, distinguish proposed changes from implemented changes and report fresh verification. Do not reopen a stage solely because human outcomes are absent.

Human and learning evidence boundary
Practitioner and affected-person review, human usability, workload, learning, retention, transfer and flourishing evidence are absent. Before any separately authorized human review, establish voluntary participation, credible passing/stopping, protected time, coverage, access, authority and suitable space. Preserve fictional inputs, no candidate telemetry or storage, no recordings, no ranking and no consequential HR advice.

Any later learning claim needs separately reviewed evidence for distinguishing facts from explanations, inviting missing accounts and identifying unresolved agreement and workflow support. Immediate supported performance, delayed retention and adaptation require distinct evidence. Copied examples, familiarity, facilitator cues, selective participation and workflow repair remain rival explanations. The optional second situation is supported practice only.

Retained dissent and accountable gate
Organizational repair, complete paper facilitation and no practice remain legitimate choices. Paper use must preserve written selection, optional speech, refusal, stopping and participant-controlled disposal without collecting or photographing sheets. Technical acceptance cannot secure these conditions. A field-use decision remains with accountable humans after the relevant evidence and conditions are reviewed.

Acceptance here authorizes neither field release nor human approval.","revision":1,"trigger_seq":34},"design":{"body":"## Problem and people

Conversation Lab proposes voluntary practice for first-time team leads using an invented missed-handoff story: a handoff note was absent on Monday, the next shift repeated a check, and the lead has not heard the colleague’s account. The task is to distinguish observation from explanation, choose an opening, reconsider changed information and prepare a feasible conversation proposal. The absent note establishes neither carelessness nor responsibility for the repeated check; their causal relationship remains unknown.

New leads, colleagues, managers, learning teams and employee representatives are prospective affected groups. None have participated. This is a revised rehearsal Design brief, not approved requirements or demonstrated proficiency. The previous workforce journal remains an immutable parent, not a measured baseline or approved intervention.

Sequence 15 integrates the specialist drafts at sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Sequence 2 preserves parent material, including a hypothetical shared-workstation interruption. Sequence 18 introduces another hypothetical event: after a template-dependent proposal exists, an authorized fictional manager offers restored access on the condition that the colleague completes the note after their shift; coverage and protected time have been withdrawn. The fictional colleague refuses the additional work. Ownership remains unresolved. Neither hypothetical event is an observation or prediction.

Rival explanations include changed schedules, inaccessible materials, unclear ownership, inadequate coverage and conflicting expectations. Conversation difficulty may be secondary to those conditions. Training is not the automatic response.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: participants need room to question observations, retain tentative interpretations, reject feedback, correct wording, withhold agreement, choose written participation, pass or stop without justification. Leads must distinguish inquiry from decisions requiring another person’s authority. A colleague’s refusal does not become a capability judgment. Managers must inspect protected time, coverage, access, ownership and suitable space. Authority to restore access does not establish authority to resolve every workflow condition or another person’s agreement. Facilitators need covered time and accessible materials; they must not grade speech, speed, confidence, eye contact or script fidelity. No resources, support owners or participation protections are secured.

System requirements: use deterministic choices and explicitly authored fictional examples. Separate source facts, possible explanations, missing accounts, initial history, current proposals and pending corrections. Represent access, relevant authority, protected capacity and agreement independently. Protected capacity comprises protected time and coverage; if either is unavailable, the combined condition is unavailable, and an unresolved component remains unknown. Do not use a single available-support label as a feasibility certificate.

Use fictional inputs only. Exclude real employee records, identifiable recordings, profiling, employee ranking, consequential HR advice, automatic scores, telemetry, storage and network requests. Keep only volatile state in the candidate frame; refresh or closure loses work. No export, sharing controls, certificates, attendance logs or aid-use records are proposed. Do not evaluate optional text or infer consent, readiness, reactions or learning needs. Humans retain consequential workplace decisions and any separate disclosure decision.

Language needs, reading demands, devices, assistive technology, suitable space and workflow resources are unknown. Responsive layout, plain wording, untimed keyboard use and visible focus are intended qualities requiring inspection. Recording nothing cannot prevent informal observation or employment pressure.

## Experience and decisions

The main task produces one conversation proposal through brief choices rather than a long questionnaire. Begin with a linear situation board labelled Observed fictional facts, Possible explanations and Missing context. Show the absent note and repeated check as observations; explanations remain tentative, including when selected. Keep the unheard colleague account and uncertain causal relationship visible. Do not rely on color, dragging, hover or spatial position.

Offer exact opening previews: “I noticed Monday’s handoff note was absent. What was happening from your perspective?”; “Can we check how the handoff was meant to work on Monday?”; and “I need more context before deciding our next step.” Choose an opening and provisional next move without mandatory typing. Pass, Stop, Cover and Paper activity remain available without reasons. Explain session loss before entry; place detailed review metadata in Help.

Each opening changes an explicitly authored possible exchange and descriptive feedback. Include a colleague offering context, questioning an interpretation or asking to discuss it later. Label dialogue beside the preview as invented possibilities, not predicted reactions or evidence about people. Participants can reject examples and feedback, retain their proposal or retry an opening against another authored possibility. No branch receives praise, blame, scores or a preferred-answer marker.

Capture the Initial proposal before revealing the supplied context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague, and the expected owner was unclear. This adds information without proving a complete cause. Invite retaining or revising the interpretation and next move. Retaining wording must still display the new constraints.

For a next move involving template use or additional handoff work, reveal relevant dependency choices: access, authority to resolve the proposed condition, and protected time/coverage, each Available, Unavailable or Unknown within the fictional prospective situation. Show what authority is needed and what work remains unassigned. Offer checking expectations, requesting support or pausing. Unknown or unavailable conditions produce a conditional proposal, inquiry or pause; they never produce an unconditional commitment. Even available support leaves reciprocal agreement unresolved.

Introduce sequence 18’s changed-condition card after a template-dependent initial proposal exists. A pending correction may remain open when the participant activates the card so the recovery rule is inspectable. Display: “Access offered; protected capacity unavailable; colleague agreement withheld; ownership unresolved.” Display the authored response: “Making the template accessible does not give me time to complete it after my shift. I cannot agree to that extra work.” Label the event and response hypothetical. An offer to restore access is distinct from confirmed availability, and neither supplies time or agreement.

After that event, offer three concrete routes: request clarification of protected capacity and ownership; reconsider the next move; or pause. Authored synthesis must leave additional work unassigned and avoid promising after-shift completion. Retaining wording or rejecting feedback remains possible, with the conflict independently visible. Prospective support changes must not erase the recorded refusal or invent later agreement. They must also leave Monday’s inaccessible template, unclear owner and the withdrawal event intact as fictional history.

Show clearly labelled Initial proposal and Current proposal. Each contains observation, invitation, next move, relevant support, authority, protected capacity, unassigned work and unresolved questions or disagreement. State neutrally what changed or was retained. Put “Fictional practice proposal; no workplace agreement or capability judgment” beside the output. On narrow screens, versions may appear sequentially with explicit labels.

Feedback describes what wording states, whose account it invites and what remains unresolved. A carelessness interpretation remains an explanation rather than an observed cause. A process inquiry identifies the expectation being checked. Template use names access, ownership and capacity conditions. Pausing leaves a suitable opportunity and agreement unarranged. Feedback is contestable; revising is not itself success.

Use at most two optional main-path text fields: replacement wording and an unresolved question, both for fictional content only. A component selector identifies what the replacement changes. Review shows the exact replacement, affected component and dependency summary before Apply or Cancel. Cancel preserves the current proposal. Applied participant wording remains verbatim and labelled; the candidate cannot certify its feasibility. Independent conditions remain visible even if the text contradicts them.

A relevant context or support change, including sequence 18’s event, invalidates any pending correction review. Preserve the draft, mark the review stale and disable Apply until the participant explicitly reviews the exact replacement with the updated conditions. Renewed review enables a separate Apply decision; reviewing alone does not apply it. Cancel preserves current wording and the newly revealed conditions rather than reversing the event.

Cover immediately conceals all content surfaces, including scenario, history, current plans, text fields, pending reviews, dialogue, second-situation progress and open detail views. Concealed content must be unavailable through ordinary assistive-technology navigation. Move focus to a neutral screen. Resume is explicit, restores current corrections and the capacity conflict, and offers optional orientation without a recall task. Stale reviews remain stale. No automatic resumption, interruption logs or inactivity assessment.

Finish and clear for handoff is separate from Cover. Describe the scope and require confirmation; Cancel retains the session. Confirmation resets every candidate value and rendered surface, including both situations, initial/current plans, support and capacity choices, refusal state, drafts and pending previews, then shows a neutral start screen. Clearing must work from Cover without revealing content. Cover retains volatile work; clearing removes candidate session state. Neither prevents prior viewing or external capture.

Offer one optional second situation: “Two shifts each understood the other to own the final checklist check.” Begin with fewer suggestions and keep help immediately available without recording its use. Produce an ownership-focused opening and next move through choices. Keep its source data and state separate: do not inherit Monday’s access barrier or sequence 18’s refusal and capacity withdrawal. Call it supported practice, not a transfer test.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Inquiry and reciprocal agency. Origins: Workforce R1/R3, sequence 5; Systems SE2, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD1/HCD2, sequence 9; Learning scientist LS1–LS3, sequence 11; integrated in sequence 15. Interaction: labelled board, distinct opening previews, contestable feedback, context reveal, optional retry and before/after proposal. Human reason: participants need to examine ambiguity without conforming to a script or losing dissent. System reason: polished examples can imply diagnosis or predicted reactions. Check: complete without typing, exercise every opening, reject examples and feedback, retain a tentative interpretation and finish with unresolved disagreement or a pause. Inspect separate second-situation facts and available support. Relevance, language and feedback criteria remain unreviewed.

R2 — Separate feasibility conditions and agreement. Origins: Workforce R2, sequence 5; Systems SE1, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD3, sequence 9; Responsible AI RA1, sequence 13; sequence 15 R2; Scenario SC1, sequence 18. Interaction: distinguish access, authority, protected capacity and agreement; introduce capacity withdrawal after an initial proposal; offer clarification, reconsideration or pause. Human reason: usable tools and managerial authority do not supply time, coverage or consent. System reason: an available-support selection can otherwise conceal an unsupported commitment. Check: available access plus unavailable capacity and withheld agreement yields qualified wording, unassigned work and unresolved ownership, without after-shift promises. Prospective support changes preserve source history and refusal. Actual resources, authority and workload arrangements remain unknown.

R3 — Correction, recovery and equivalent alternatives. Origins: hypothetical interruption preserved at sequence 2; Workforce R4/R5, sequence 5; Systems SE3/SE4, sequence 7; Human-centered designer HCD4/HCD5, sequence 9; Learning scientist LS4, sequence 11; Responsible AI RA2–RA4, sequence 13; sequence 15 R3; Scenario SC1, sequence 18. Interaction: exact review/Apply/Cancel, stale-review handling, complete Cover, explicit Resume, confirmed handoff clearing and direct paper access. Human reason: interruption and dissent require control without memory tests or loss of refusal. System reason: stale previews and partial resets can expose or restore rejected content. Check: introduce withdrawal during review, require renewed inspection, cancel without reversing the event, cover/resume the corrected state and confirm complete clearing from Cover. Inspect keyboard focus, concealment, narrow layout and prohibited technical behavior. Run the full paper task. No checks have occurred.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Choices reduce entry burden but constrain expression; optional correction and unresolved questions preserve another route. Examples support participation but can invite imitation; rejecting them and requesting help remain legitimate. Dependency details add work, so reveal them when the next move requires them. Before/after comparison makes revision inspectable without rewarding change.

Retain dissent that organizational repair or no practice is preferable. An accountable review of rota, coverage, protected time, ownership and accessible materials is a non-learning option. The candidate cannot authorize repairs. Deterministic browser practice and facilitated paper practice are non-AI options; neither secures participation protections.

Complete paper materials: a situation card containing the three initial story statements; a board labelled Observed facts, Possible explanations and Missing context; the three exact opening cards above; blank replacement, Pass and Stop cards. A reveal card states the changed rota, inaccessible template and unclear owner, labelled invented context rather than a complete cause. Authored response cards say “Here is additional context”, “I question that interpretation” and “I would prefer to discuss this later”, labelled possibilities rather than predictions.

Provide Initial proposal and Current proposal sheets with spaces for observation, invitation, next move, access, authority, protected time/coverage, agreement, unassigned work and unresolved questions. Supply Available, Unavailable and Unknown cards for support conditions; agreement remains separately unresolved or withheld. Add sequence 18’s complete changed-condition card and exact refusal above. Add a feedback card asking: “Which wording is observation or explanation?”, “Whose account or agreement is missing?” and “What support makes the move feasible?” Include a blank cover sheet and the exact second-situation card, with opening suggestions available on request.

Facilitation: arrange voluntary participation, protected time, accessible materials, suitable space and participant-controlled disposal first. Present the situation, invite an opening or Pass, and record the initial proposal. Release the reveal; for a template-dependent proposal, release the changed-condition card after the initial plan exists. Preserve refusal and leave additional work unassigned. Invite retention, one-component revision or stopping; describe implications without grading. Show the exact replacement and conditions before accepting it; cancellation preserves the current sheet. If conditions change during review, review again before acceptance. Offer an optional response-card retry or the separate second situation. Written selection is sufficient; speech and role-play are optional. Cover for interruption and resume only by participant choice. Do not solicit personal accounts, collect or photograph sheets, grade aid use, record attendance for assessment or require sharing. Dispose under the participant-controlled arrangement. These conditions are not secured.

## Acceptance checks

Plan fictional task walkthroughs for all openings, retained interpretations, rejected feedback, inaccessible templates, disputed ownership and postponed discussion. Complete with blank optional fields. Inspect faithful source distinctions, useful output and absence of scores or implied agreement.

Plan a capacity and recovery walkthrough: preserve an initial template proposal, open correction review, reveal sequence 18’s event, inspect stale-review handling and qualified output, renew review, cancel, cover and resume. Inspect preserved refusal and current wording; cancel clearing once, then confirm from Cover and inspect both situations and all state reset. Separately inspect keyboard behavior, concealed accessibility content, responsive layout, code and runtime for storage, tracking and network requests. These are planned checks, not observed behavior.

Pending practitioner, affected-person and representative review must examine comprehension, credible refusal, reciprocal dignity, belonging, language, device access, sustainable workload, screen visibility and paper handling. Technical verification would establish only inspected behavior, not free participation, learning, retention, transfer or flourishing.

## Evidence and unknowns

Sequence 15 supplies the previous integrated Design and its specialist origins; sequence 18 supplies the hypothetical capacity conflict. Neither is empirical evidence. Sequence 2’s preservation event does not approve the preserved material. No participant observations, consensus, human approval, technical results, field pilot or empirical success exists. Field evidence remains pending.

The concrete change from sequence 15 is independent protected-capacity representation, an actionable withdrawal/refusal state, renewed correction review and complete recovery coverage of those values. Preserve its inquiry, access, authority, disagreement and paper requirements. Design is the earliest supplied interaction artifact invalidated by this event; the material does not establish an omission in Map.

Unknowns include task relevance, local shift arrangements, authority to secure protected time, credible refusal, acceptable feedback and added burden. Apparent improvement could reflect copied examples, familiarity, facilitator cues, selective participation or repaired workflow. Difficulty could reflect language, reading demands, workload or dissent rather than a capability deficit. Immediate supported performance, delayed retention and adaptation in changed workplace conditions require different evidence; none is established here.

## Next decision

Replace sequence 15’s Design brief with this targeted revision, then implement a focused deterministic rehearsal Build. Exercise the planned fictional technical cases and prepare practitioner and affected-person interaction review. Keep intended quality, subsequently observed technical behavior and untested learning and flourishing separate. This is one Design revision, with no request to reopen Map.
